title: Nuclear Medicine Residency
prerequisites: MD/DO-level foundational knowledge or equivalent supervised health-professional background is assumed for the clinical concepts.

For board-eligibility context, ABNM describes a preparatory clinical year with at least nine months of direct patient care before nuclear medicine training; this course neither verifies nor supplies it.
Basic algebra, SI units, probability/statistics and cross-sectional-anatomy familiarity are useful.
Learners must not handle radiopharmaceuticals, supervise stress testing, direct patient imaging, interpret clinical studies independently or make treatment decisions through this course.
objectives: Map independent study to the current public ABNM in-training domain taxonomy without claiming exam equivalence.
Explain core nuclear-medicine physics, radiopharmacy, instrumentation, PET/SPECT and hybrid-imaging quality concepts.
Use a cautious, mechanism-to-correlation reasoning structure for cardiovascular, pediatric/pulmonary, endocrine, GI/GU, musculoskeletal, neuro, oncologic and therapy topics.
Recognize evidence and governance qualifiers in cardiac amyloid imaging and modern theranostics.
Identify when a question requires qualified, supervised clinical and regulatory review rather than self-study action.

units.title: Scope, clinical foundations, radiation safety and regulatory boundaries
objectives: Differentiate self-study from supervised clinical residency and authorized-user training.
Explain why patient safety, dose optimization, verification and escalation remain supervised clinical responsibilities.
topics: Course limits; ACGME/ABNM training distinction; radiation quantities and protection principles; safety-event vocabulary; evidence retrieval.
units.casePractice: Compare an explicitly fictional referral with the information a supervised service would need; identify what cannot be completed in self-study.
units.assessment: Five-item boundaries-and-safety quiz plus a source-annotated reflection.

units.title: Radionuclides, radiopharmacy, tracer kinetics and dosimetry
objectives: Relate decay, emission, targeting and biodistribution to image signal and radiation burden.
Recognize why preparation, QC and patient-specific decisions require authorized workflows.
topics: Radioactive decay; radiopharmaceutical development; kinetics; counting statistics; absorbed-dose concepts; radiopharmacy QC.
units.casePractice: Work through fictional tracer-selection and unexpected-biodistribution prompts without prescribing an administration.
units.assessment: Calculation concepts quiz; label each conclusion as observation, differential, or escalation.

units.title: Instrumentation, reconstruction, artifacts and quality control
objectives: Explain how gamma cameras, SPECT, PET/CT and dose calibrators produce and distort data.
Use a structured QC-first approach to potential artifact without treating a learner response as a clinical sign-off.
topics: Detectors; collimation; attenuation/scatter; PET performance; CT correlation; image registration; daily QC; reconstruction artifacts.
units.casePractice: Annotate a conceptual PET/CT misregistration diagram and draft a non-clinical QC escalation checklist.
units.assessment: Artifact-identification worksheet and a short oral explanation.

units.title: Hybrid imaging and reporting logic: PET/CT, SPECT/CT and correlation
objectives: Sequence identity, indication, acquisition adequacy, physiologic uptake, pathology and limitation checks.
Distinguish a diagnostic PSMA PET selection study from post-therapy Lu-177 imaging.
topics: PET/CT; SPECT/CT; registration; attenuation correction; correlative CT; structured report elements; physiologic uptake and pitfalls.
units.casePractice: Compare two fictional modality requests and state what clinical question each can and cannot answer.
units.assessment: One structured fictional report template with uncertainty and comparison fields.

units.title: Cardiovascular nuclear medicine
objectives: Describe the roles of stress supervision, myocardial perfusion imaging and PET/SPECT in cardiovascular evaluation.
Apply the key qualification that bone-avid amyloid scans require monoclonal-protein evaluation and SPECT context.
topics: Stress testing; myocardial perfusion; viability concepts; gated imaging; cardiac PET; amyloid scintigraphy; artifacts.
units.casePractice: Use a fictional cardiac referral to list clinical-context questions and the evidence required before interpreting myocardial uptake.
units.assessment: Cardiac protocols-and-pitfalls quiz; no patient-specific recommendation.

units.title: Pediatric and pulmonary nuclear medicine
objectives: Recognize pediatric-specific need for indication, protocol review and radiation-aware practice.
Organize differential reasoning for lung perfusion, reflux/aspiration, renal and bone scintigraphy.
topics: Pediatric imaging safeguards; lung perfusion; reflux/aspiration; cortical renal scintigraphy; cystography; pediatric bone imaging.
units.casePractice: Classify fictional prompts by likely study category and missing pre-imaging information, without selecting a patient dose.
units.assessment: Six-station matching exercise and a safety pause checklist.

units.title: Endocrine nuclear medicine and iodine-based imaging/therapy principles
objectives: Interpret the conceptual relationship among thyroid physiology, scintigraphy and whole-body imaging.
Identify why treatment decisions, contraindication checks and administered activities are not self-study tasks.
topics: Thyroid and parathyroid scintigraphy; hyperthyroidism and thyroid cancer concepts; I-131 imaging; therapy/dosimetry concepts; pediatric thyroid imaging.
units.casePractice: Draft a fictional-image observation list that separates physiologic uptake, technical limitation and clinical correlation.
units.assessment: Endocrine case conference with a source-anchored limitations section.

units.title: Gastrointestinal and genitourinary studies
objectives: Map clinical questions to physiologic nuclear-medicine study families.
Recognize the importance of acquisition adequacy and correlation before inference.
topics: Reflux/aspiration; hepatobiliary and gastric concepts; renal cortical imaging; obstruction/reflux concepts; transplant and pediatric considerations.
units.casePractice: Review linked case resources at their source and record only observations and differentials in a personal worksheet.
units.assessment: Ten-item modality/physiology map and a fictional renal-scan reasoning note.

units.title: Musculoskeletal, infection/inflammation and bone turnover
objectives: Use mechanism-first reasoning for osseous tracer uptake and common pitfalls.
State why uptake pattern alone is not a diagnosis without clinical, anatomic and temporal context.
topics: Bone remodeling; bone scintigraphy; pediatric bone; infection/inflammation concepts; metastatic patterns; hybrid correlation.
units.casePractice: Make a differential matrix for a fictional focal osseous uptake pattern, including benign and technical alternatives.
units.assessment: Pattern-and-pitfall quiz with justification and a limitation statement.

units.title: Neurology and oncologic molecular imaging
objectives: Describe how tracer biology, acquisition and correlation influence neuro and oncologic PET interpretation.
Use cautious language for physiologic variants and therapy-response questions.
topics: Brain PET concepts; FDG PET/CT; oncology; physiologic variants; lymphoma/infection concepts; quantitation limitations; correlative imaging.
units.casePractice: Create an evidence table for a fictional PET/CT report: indication, expected biodistribution, finding, differential, limitation and next clinical review.
units.assessment: Original 12-item PET/CT case-based quiz; explanation must cite an open guideline or primary source.

units.title: Theranostics, radionuclide therapy and post-therapy imaging
objectives: Explain the conceptual pairing of target expression imaging, treatment eligibility, radiation safety and follow-up imaging.
Distinguish current FDA indication language from a general claim that all symptomatic bone metastases or all uptake patterns are treated.
topics: I-131; Lu-177 PSMA; Lu-177 dotatate; radium-223 qualification; dosimetry; adverse-effect monitoring concepts; post-treatment SPECT/CT is distinct from selection PET.
units.casePractice: Use fictional referrals to identify eligibility facts that are missing; do not select therapy, dose or a management plan.
units.assessment: Theranostics evidence brief, graded on indication qualification, safety boundaries and citation quality.

units.title: Integrated interpretation, communication, quality improvement and board-oriented synthesis
objectives: Synthesize technical, physiologic, clinical and evidence limits in a structured interpretation approach.
Build an independent study plan aligned to ABNM domains without representing it as a board-approved curriculum.
topics: Protocol verification; reporting; communication; error and discrepancy learning; evidence appraisal; blueprint-weighted review; exam strategy limits.
units.casePractice: Complete a fictional multidisciplinary handoff in which uncertainty, technical quality and escalation are explicit.
units.assessment: Cumulative original 50-question formative assessment and a reflective learning plan.

assignment.title: Fictional case-and-evidence portfolio
assignment.instructions: Complete six explicitly fictional study prompts spanning a technical artifact, cardiac referral, pediatric/pulmonary question, endocrine question, PET/CT oncology question and therapy eligibility question. For each, state indication, technical adequacy checks, expected biodistribution/mechanism, differential, limitations, correlative information needed and escalation boundary. Cite at least one current primary guideline, regulator or board source. Do not use identifiable images, copied proprietary questions, actual patient records or patient-specific recommendations.
deliverables: Six 250-400 word structured observations
One one-page source update log
One ethics/licensing attestation for any linked case
assignment.gradingPlan: Formative rubric: 30% technical reasoning; 25% mechanism and physiology; 25% limitations/escalation; 20% source quality. No clinical sign-off.

assessment.format: Formative only: unit quizzes, structured fictional case observations, source checks and cumulative original questions.
assessment.passingClaim: No score is a predictor of ABNM/ABR performance, clinical competence, eligibility or passing.
assessment.integrity: All questions below are original educational items, not recalled, leaked or proprietary board questions.

mapping.name: Nuclear Medicine Residency Program
mapping.publicCurriculumNotes: Johns Hopkins publicly lists an ACGME-accredited three-year program and states that it qualifies trainees to sit the ABNM exam. Its detailed radiology page describes diagnostic and therapeutic teaching and variable duration based on prior training. The public pages do not provide a complete rotation schedule, case log, conference calendar or lecture-duration ledger.

mapping.name: Nuclear Medicine Residency
mapping.publicCurriculumNotes: Emory publicly describes adult and pediatric nuclear medicine, molecular imaging, complex radionuclide therapies, multiple clinical settings, didactics, conferences and research. It describes different durations by prior training. The public page is descriptive and does not publish a complete lecture ledger, full rotation calendar or case-volume evidence.

unitMap.text: Scope, clinical foundations, radiation safety and regulatory boundaries
coveredTopics: Course limits; ACGME/ABNM training distinction; radiation quantities and protection principles; safety-event vocabulary; evidence retrieval.

unitMap.text: Radionuclides, radiopharmacy, tracer kinetics and dosimetry
coveredTopics: Radioactive decay; radiopharmaceutical development; kinetics; counting statistics; absorbed-dose concepts; radiopharmacy QC.

unitMap.text: Instrumentation, reconstruction, artifacts and quality control
coveredTopics: Detectors; collimation; attenuation/scatter; PET performance; CT correlation; image registration; daily QC; reconstruction artifacts.

unitMap.text: Hybrid imaging and reporting logic: PET/CT, SPECT/CT and correlation
coveredTopics: PET/CT; SPECT/CT; registration; attenuation correction; correlative CT; structured report elements; physiologic uptake and pitfalls.

unitMap.text: Cardiovascular nuclear medicine
coveredTopics: Stress testing; myocardial perfusion; viability concepts; gated imaging; cardiac PET; amyloid scintigraphy; artifacts.

unitMap.text: Pediatric and pulmonary nuclear medicine
coveredTopics: Pediatric imaging safeguards; lung perfusion; reflux/aspiration; cortical renal scintigraphy; cystography; pediatric bone imaging.

unitMap.text: Endocrine nuclear medicine and iodine-based imaging/therapy principles
coveredTopics: Thyroid and parathyroid scintigraphy; hyperthyroidism and thyroid cancer concepts; I-131 imaging; therapy/dosimetry concepts; pediatric thyroid imaging.

unitMap.text: Gastrointestinal and genitourinary studies
coveredTopics: Reflux/aspiration; hepatobiliary and gastric concepts; renal cortical imaging; obstruction/reflux concepts; transplant and pediatric considerations.

unitMap.text: Musculoskeletal, infection/inflammation and bone turnover
coveredTopics: Bone remodeling; bone scintigraphy; pediatric bone; infection/inflammation concepts; metastatic patterns; hybrid correlation.

unitMap.text: Neurology and oncologic molecular imaging
coveredTopics: Brain PET concepts; FDG PET/CT; oncology; physiologic variants; lymphoma/infection concepts; quantitation limitations; correlative imaging.

unitMap.text: Theranostics, radionuclide therapy and post-therapy imaging
coveredTopics: I-131; Lu-177 PSMA; Lu-177 dotatate; radium-223 qualification; dosimetry; adverse-effect monitoring concepts; post-treatment SPECT/CT is distinct from selection PET.

unitMap.text: Integrated interpretation, communication, quality improvement and board-oriented synthesis
coveredTopics: Protocol verification; reporting; communication; error and discrepancy learning; evidence appraisal; blueprint-weighted review; exam strategy limits.

topicGaps: The observed 36-hour floor is met: 68 unique free-to-view recordings total 37.506667 verified hours (27.505000 foundation; 10.001667 specialty). This does not demonstrate board readiness or clinical competence.

The expanded ledger is still uneven. It now contains extensive technical physics, detectors, reconstruction, QA/QC and dosimetry; specialty video coverage remains selected rather than a complete clinical lecture series.

Insufficient open long-form video coverage remains for adult hepatobiliary/gastric GI, broader adult GU beyond obstruction renography, musculoskeletal infection/inflammation, comprehensive adult oncologic PET, broader neuro PET, and supervised therapy operations/reporting. These are explicit original-production plans, not verified recordings.

Johns Hopkins and Emory program pages are descriptive and do not publish a complete lecture ledger, rotation schedule, case log or all didactics. No institutional private course material, proprietary case volume, patient image, supervised clinical service, radiation-safety authorization or board-approved simulation is included.

ABNM domain mapping and question weights are a dated public blueprint snapshot. This independent course does not establish ABNM eligibility, ACGME completion, licensure, NRC/Agreement State authorization, clinical competence or certification; human clinician review of this expansion has not been performed.
remainingGaps.clinicalSkills: Supervised accredited clinical training is not supplied by these videos.

boardNames: American Board of Nuclear Medicine (ABNM)

boardStatus.status: ABNM is the relevant US physician specialty certification board for this primary nuclear medicine residency track. Its certification exam and in-training blueprint are mapped here for independent study only.
boardStatus.blueprintScope: The ABNM published in-training blueprint has 10 major classifications: Core, Cardiovascular, Endocrine, Gastrointestinal, Genitourinary, Musculoskeletal / Infection-Inflammation, Neurology, Oncology, Pulmonary and Therapy; Oncology is 34% in the published 125-question in-training blueprint.
boardStatus.notASeparateFellowshipBoardClaim: This course does not represent a nuclear radiology or PET/CT fellowship, and it makes no separate-board claim for any fellowship.

medical.boardEligibilityNotice: Independent self-study cannot establish ABNM eligibility, ACGME completion, physician licensure, NRC/Agreement State authorized-user status, supervised procedure/case experience, clinical competence or board certification. ABNM eligibility depends on qualifying education/training, program verification and other current requirements. Consult ABNM, ACGME and the local regulatory program directly.

officialProgrammes.name: Nuclear Medicine Residency Program
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: Johns Hopkins publicly lists an ACGME-accredited three-year program and states that it qualifies trainees to sit the ABNM exam. The public pages do not provide a complete rotation schedule, case log, conference calendar or lecture-duration ledger.

It describes different durations by prior training. The public page is descriptive and does not publish a complete lecture ledger, full rotation calendar or case-volume evidence.

medical.programmeSourceScope: Institutional pages establish that these are clinical physician training programmes and describe broad scope. They are not a substitute for ACGME requirements, ABNM eligibility rules or a complete public curriculum; no proprietary lecture set, training volume, equipment claim beyond the current official page, or unverified user-outline benchmark is imported.
sourceCaveats: All programme, board, guideline and FDA pages were fetched/opened on 2026-10-07. Indications, labels, standards, eligibility and blueprints can change; consult current primary documents before use.

Lecture durations are observed public metadata, not estimates. Each unique YouTube video ID is counted once. Spanish-language duplicates and non-substantive institutional-information content were excluded.

The channel was public, but automated full-media extraction encountered YouTube anti-bot responses for some items. No protected access was attempted. The ledger counts the observed publicly listed recordings; users should confirm watch-page availability themselves.
Radiopaedia and MedPix are linked, not copied. Free viewing is not blanket reuse permission. No authentic case/image is included in the files.

The supplied outline was treated as unverified: no claimed top-percentile case volumes, dual-board claims, exact service volumes, proprietary equipment assertions, or broad therapy indications were imported.

Separate preparation, acquisition adequacy, normal transit, abnormal transit and clinical differential without issuing patient-specific interpretation.
scriptOutline: Build a tracer-to-physiology map from an official procedure standard and open clinical reference.

Work through an explicitly fictional teaching prompt without a synthetic diagnostic image.

Use a fictional pattern-matching exercise without diagnostic images.

topicGaps: The observed 36-hour floor is met: 68 unique free-to-view recordings total 37.506667 verified hours (27.505000 foundation; 10.001667 specialty). This does not demonstrate board readiness or clinical competence.

The expanded ledger is still uneven. It now contains extensive technical physics, detectors, reconstruction, QA/QC and dosimetry; specialty video coverage remains selected rather than a complete clinical lecture series.

Insufficient open long-form video coverage remains for adult hepatobiliary/gastric GI, broader adult GU beyond obstruction renography, musculoskeletal infection/inflammation, comprehensive adult oncologic PET, broader neuro PET, and supervised therapy operations/reporting. These are explicit original-production plans, not verified recordings.

Johns Hopkins and Emory program pages are descriptive and do not publish a complete lecture ledger, rotation schedule, case log or all didactics. No institutional private course material, proprietary case volume, patient image, supervised clinical service, radiation-safety authorization or board-approved simulation is included.

ABNM domain mapping and question weights are a dated public blueprint snapshot. This independent course does not establish ABNM eligibility, ACGME completion, licensure, NRC/Agreement State authorization, clinical competence or certification; human clinician review of this expansion has not been performed.
medical.sourceReviewNote: Source-cited research and automated checks; not clinician validation or exam-passing prediction.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement most accurately describes this independent course in relation to ABNM certification eligibility?

options.text: Completing the lectures satisfies the ABNM residency-training requirement.
It can replace supervised clinical work if the learner completes a final quiz.
It is self-study that may support knowledge review but does not supply the accredited/supervised training required for eligibility.
It grants authorized-user status after 36 video hours.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABNM eligibility requires qualifying training and program verification; ACGME requirements include supervised patient care and assessment. Video self-study cannot substitute for either.

practiceQuestions.stem: Before starting a US nuclear medicine residency pathway, which preparatory clinical training feature is specifically described by ABNM?

options.text: One year that includes at least nine months of direct patient care.
Thirty-six hours of online radiation safety video.
A diagnostic-radiology fellowship only.
A research year without clinical duties.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABNM states that preparatory clinical training before nuclear medicine training includes one year with at least nine months in a specialty providing direct patient care.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional patient has a bone-avid cardiac scan with myocardial uptake visually at least as intense as rib uptake. Which additional evaluation is essential to qualify an ATTR interpretation rather than calling the scan alone pathognomonic?

options.text: Serum and urine immunofixation plus serum free light-chain testing.
PI-RADS scoring.
A post-therapy Lu-177 scan.
No further evaluation because uptake alone proves ATTR.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ASNC/EANM practice points state that grade 2 or 3 uptake is strongly suggestive, but AL amyloidosis can show uptake; a monoclonal process must be excluded with serum/urine immunofixation and serum free light-chain testing.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement correctly distinguishes a PSMA PET selection study from post-treatment Lu-177 imaging?

options.text: They are interchangeable because both show radiotracer distribution.
PSMA PET can be used for tumor-expression-based selection under approved-product labeling; post-treatment imaging has its own SPECT/CT-focused guideline purpose.
Post-treatment imaging replaces all pretreatment eligibility assessment.
Neither has a role in molecular imaging.

practiceQuestions.rationale: FDA describes approved PSMA PET selection for Pluvicto based on tumor PSMA expression, whereas SNMMI/ACNM publish specific recommendations for post-treatment SPECT/CT after Lu-177 therapies. They address different clinical questions.

practiceQuestions.stem: As of the cited March 2025 FDA notice, which fictional candidate most closely matches the expanded Pluvicto indication described there?

options.text: An adult with PSMA-positive mCRPC previously treated with an androgen-receptor pathway inhibitor and considered appropriate to delay taxane chemotherapy.
Any patient with a painful bone metastasis, regardless of cancer type or PSMA status.
A patient with an indeterminate thyroid nodule.
A patient selected only by post-therapy imaging.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The March 2025 FDA notice describes adults with PSMA-positive mCRPC treated with ARPI who are appropriate to delay taxane chemotherapy. The source does not support the broader alternatives. Eligibility and treatment are clinician-supervised decisions.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement matches the cited April 2024 FDA information for lutetium Lu 177 dotatate?

options.text: It was approved only for imaging traumatic bone injury.
It applies to all neuroendocrine tumors without receptor qualification.
FDA approved it for pediatric patients 12 years and older with SSTR-positive gastroenteropancreatic NETs, in addition to the adult indication context described by FDA.
It is a substitute for an amyloid scan.

practiceQuestions.rationale: FDA’s April 2024 notice describes the pediatric approval for patients 12 years and older with SSTR-positive GEP-NETs. The label/source must be checked for current details; this question does not provide treatment advice.

practiceQuestions.stem: In a fictional PET/CT review, an apparent focus aligns poorly with the CT anatomy and shifts between fused views. What is the best initial learning response?

options.text: Call it malignant immediately.
First consider registration/acquisition and technical artifact, then seek supervised clinical review and correlation.
Ignore the CT component.
Use a renal cyst classification system.

practiceQuestions.rationale: PET/CT registration accuracy and daily QC are specific technical concerns in the observed IAEA lessons. A mismatch should trigger technical review and correlation, not unsupported diagnostic certainty.

practiceQuestions.stem: A learner sees focal skeletal tracer uptake in a fictional case. Which reporting habit is most defensible?

options.text: Declare a single diagnosis from uptake alone.
Use mechanism, distribution, clinical context, correlative imaging and technical factors to form a differential and state limitations.
Apply LI-RADS to the skeletal focus.
Assume all uptake represents infection.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Bone turnover and musculoskeletal scintigraphy require mechanism and correlation. The ABNM content taxonomy includes artifact, malignancy, inflammation/infection and other processes; uptake alone is not a diagnosis.

practiceQuestions.stem: What proportion of the published ABNM in-training blueprint is classified as Oncology?
practiceQuestions.rationale: The published ABNM in-training blueprint lists Oncology as 43 of 125 questions, or 34%. This is a mapping aid, not a promise that another exam or future blueprint will be identical.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which activity may not be counted as the minimum 200 hours of classroom and laboratory training in radiation safety and safe handling under the ABNM training-requirements summary?

options.text: Reviewing case histories or interpreting scans.
Relevant classroom or laboratory instruction meeting the specified subject matter.
Training that is part of qualifying supervised requirements.
An activity documented by a qualifying program under the applicable rules.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABNM explicitly states that reviewing case histories or interpreting scans should not be counted toward the minimum 200 hours of classroom/laboratory radiation-safety and handling training. This course cannot document regulatory credit.

title: Nuclear Radiology Fellowship
prerequisites: Intended level: physicians who have completed or are completing diagnostic-radiology training, or other learners using it strictly for conceptual self-study.
Working knowledge of cross-sectional anatomy, radiopharmaceutical basics and radiation-safety principles is assumed.

Clinical application requires appropriate licensing, supervision, institutional credentialing and radiation-safety authorization; self-study access has no clinical prerequisite but gives no clinical permission.
objectives: Apply published ABR topic categories to a transparent study sequence.
Explain PET, SPECT/CT and radiopharmaceutical principles and technical limitations.
Use differential-first, uncertainty-aware reasoning for common nuclear-radiology applications.
Distinguish programme pages, board requirements, FDA labels and guidelines by source type.
Recognize therapy indication qualifiers and the boundary between diagnostic selection and therapy administration.
Use PYP/DPD/HMDP cardiac-amyloid safeguards without calling uptake alone pathognomonic for ATTR.
Respect image provenance, de-identification, copyright and licence constraints.
State why supervised clinical training and authorized-user requirements cannot be fulfilled by online study.

units.title: Physics, radionuclides and quantitative foundations
objectives: Connect decay, photon interactions and detector behavior to image quality.
Explain tracer production and measured-activity uncertainty without using patient-specific dosing.
topics: PET coincidence detection; radionuclide production; counts/statistics; internal-dosimetry concepts
boardDomains: ABR Physics and Radioisotope Safety: radiation physics/instrumentation; mathematics; chemistry; radiation biology
units.casePractice: Synthetic count-statistics and decay exercises only; no patient-specific dose calculation.
units.assessment: Original questions Q06 and Q08 plus a source-cited physics concept map.

units.title: Instrumentation, quality control and artefact reasoning
objectives: Identify when a technical concern should lead to QC review rather than biological over-interpretation.
Describe PET/CT registration and QC concepts at a systems level.
topics: PET/CT registration; QC; harmonisation; bone turnover as a tracer-physiology anchor
boardDomains: ABR Physics and Radioisotope Safety: instrumentation; radiation protection
units.casePractice: For each linked case, record acquisition/registration uncertainty before proposing a differential; do not download or rehost images.
units.assessment: Short technical-error checklist, reviewed against IAEA QA reading.

units.title: Hybrid imaging and structured correlation
objectives: Integrate functional uptake with CT/MR anatomy and state limits of co-registration.
Use a structured observation-to-impression workflow rather than uptake alone.
topics: PET/CT; SPECT/CT; attenuation correction; incidental CT findings; report structure
boardDomains: ABR Clinical Nuclear Radiology: neoplasms, infection/inflammation; Physics: instrumentation
units.casePractice: Complete the IAEA standalone SPECT/CT module; its duration is unknown and is not counted in verified video hours.
units.assessment: Write a fictional structured report with technical adequacy, findings, limitations and suggested correlation.

units.title: Oncologic PET/CT and molecular imaging evidence
objectives: Recognize that FDG uptake is not cancer-specific and frame imaging in clinical context.
Distinguish diagnostic PSMA PET selection from post-therapy imaging.
topics: FDG appropriateness; tumour biology; PSMA PET; somatostatin-receptor imaging; response limitations
units.casePractice: Use the IAEA FDG PET/CT standalone module and a TCIA collection only after checking its specific licence and DOI.
units.assessment: Original questions Q03 and Q10; one evidence-to-claim audit.

units.title: Neurologic and inflammatory applications
objectives: Relate a molecular-imaging finding to a differential rather than a single diagnosis.
State why clinical history, anatomic imaging and artefact review remain necessary.
topics: Brain PET foundations; neurodegeneration patterns; infection/inflammation reasoning
boardDomains: ABR Clinical Nuclear Radiology: central nervous system; infection/inflammation
units.casePractice: Linked-only review of IAEA e-learning or MedPix cases; retain no patient material.
units.assessment: Fictional differential table with source-cited limitations.

units.title: Nuclear cardiology and cardiac amyloidosis safeguards
objectives: Describe stress-study supervision as a clinical-training requirement, not a self-study substitute.
Interpret bone-avid tracer findings with SPECT confirmation and monoclonal-protein exclusion safeguards.
topics: Stress protocols; perfusion concepts; ATTR/AL distinction; PYP/DPD/HMDP visual grading; blood-pool pitfall
boardDomains: ABR Clinical Nuclear Radiology: cardiovascular system
units.casePractice: Use fictional cases only: annotate whether SPECT localization and monoclonal-protein evaluation are present before any conclusion.
units.assessment: Original questions Q01, Q02 and Q09.

units.title: Pulmonary, renal, gastrointestinal and skeletal studies
objectives: Organize indication, physiologic question, acquisition limitation and differential for common non-oncologic studies.
Recognize the added interpretive responsibility of hybrid anatomic correlation.
topics: Renal cortical imaging; cystography; lung perfusion; GI aspiration/reflux; bone scintigraphy
boardDomains: ABR Clinical Nuclear Radiology: pulmonary; gastrointestinal; genitourinary; musculoskeletal
units.casePractice: IAEA case modules are linked for independent review; duration is deliberately uncounted unless measured.
units.assessment: Four fictional protocol-selection rationales, each ending with a limitation statement.

units.title: Endocrine imaging, thyroid disease and radioiodine context
objectives: Separate thyroid/parathyroid imaging interpretation from treatment authorization.
Identify why I-131 imaging, therapy planning and follow-up require supervised local protocols.
topics: Thyroid/parathyroid scintigraphy; I-131 whole-body imaging; benign and malignant thyroid disease; follow-up pitfalls
boardDomains: ABR Clinical Nuclear Radiology: endocrine/reproductive; therapies
units.casePractice: Use linked IAEA thyroid content as a study source, not as a treatment protocol.
units.assessment: Original question Q06 and a fictional report-quality rubric.

units.title: Paediatric nuclear medicine
objectives: State why paediatric cases require age-appropriate context and supervision.
Compare paediatric clinical questions across bone, renal, lung, GI and thyroid studies.
topics: Paediatric bone; renal; thyroid; lung perfusion; myocardial perfusion; GI aspiration
boardDomains: ABR Clinical Nuclear Radiology: paediatric applications across organ systems
units.casePractice: Use IAEA paediatric clinical-case resource by link only; never reproduce case images without rights review.
units.assessment: Fictional paediatric-case safety and differential checklist.

units.title: Radiopharmaceutical therapy and theranostics
objectives: Differentiate diagnostic target-expression imaging from therapeutic administration.
Summarize current labelled indications without converting them into patient-specific recommendations.
topics: Theranostics; Lu-177 PSMA; Lu-177 dotatate; Ra-223; I-131; adverse-effect and team-based safeguards
boardDomains: ABR Clinical Nuclear Radiology: therapies, oral and parenteral; Physics/Safety: written-directive procedures
units.casePractice: Map each fictional referral to “diagnostic evidence needed,” “label/guideline needs checking,” and “multidisciplinary decision”; no treatment calculation.
units.assessment: Original questions Q03, Q04, Q05 and Q10.

units.title: Radiation safety, regulation and professional boundaries
objectives: Explain why classroom knowledge cannot create authorized-user status.
Describe the role of supervised experience, programme verification and local radiation-safety procedures.
topics: NRC-linked training; written-directive categories; contamination response concepts; medical-event prevention; documentation
boardDomains: ABR Physics and Radioisotope Safety: radiation protection; NRC-related topics; written-directive procedures
units.casePractice: Tabletop, fictional spill/administration-prevention scenario only; no real workflow authorization.
units.assessment: Original questions Q07 and Q08 plus a scope-of-practice reflection.

units.title: Evidence appraisal, reporting, multidisciplinary communication and capstone
objectives: Produce a source-cited, uncertainty-aware fictional imaging impression.
Audit a claim against label, guideline, board and programme source types.
topics: Evidence hierarchy; report communication; limitations; image provenance; consent/de-identification; case conference reasoning
boardDomains: Integrated ABR clinical and physics/safety domains; no claim of an official blueprint match beyond S4
units.casePractice: Capstone uses only fictional vignettes or linked, lawfully accessible cases with source and licence recorded.
units.assessment: Ten-question original bank, source audit, and one fictional multidisciplinary summary.

assignment.title: Source-audited fictional case conference
requirements: Select two fictional vignettes and one linked, lawfully accessible public case resource; do not copy or rehost images.
For each vignette record the clinical question, modality limitation, differential, relevant source type, and a sentence that avoids diagnostic certainty beyond evidence.
For one therapy vignette, cite a current FDA/authoritative source and identify what must be verified at point of care.
For one cardiac vignette, show the SPECT-localization and monoclonal-protein safeguards.
assignment.submissionBoundary: Educational work only. No patient data, treatment recommendation, protocol authorization, dose calculation or procedure sign-off.

topicGaps: The observed accessible free recording ledger is 15.573611 hours, leaving 20.426389 hours below the 36-hour target; no new recording in this audit met both free public access and observed-runtime requirements.

Adult oncologic PET/CT interpretation, non-FDG tracers, appropriateness, response assessment, structured reporting and infection/inflammation remain without a complete duration-verified public teaching sequence; episode MED-002-EXPLAIN-002 teaches only an introductory reasoning framework.

The ASNC/EANM safeguards are sourceable, but there is no verified long-form public recording that covers the complete cardiac amyloidosis domain; episode MED-002-EXPLAIN-003 does not replace current protocol or expert review.

Theranostics patient selection, indications, toxicity management, longitudinal monitoring, post-therapy imaging and multidisciplinary practice lack a complete current duration-verified series; episode MED-002-EXPLAIN-004 is a limited label-reading lesson, not a clinical curriculum.

Required hands-on radiation-safety, written-directive experience, authorized-user attestation and supervised patient care cannot be supplied by self-study or online video; episode MED-002-EXPLAIN-005 explains boundaries only.

Public AAR lecture catalogue lists relevant talks but no accessible per-video runtime ledger was verified. Stanford’s recorded lecture library explicitly requires SUNet login; these items remain uncounted.
Public Emory and Harvard-affiliated programme pages do not expose the full proprietary curriculum, lecture set, rotation schedule, procedure logs or case volumes.
remainingGaps.clinicalSkills: Supervised accredited clinical training is not supplied by these videos.

medical.boardStatus: ABR Nuclear Radiology is an ABR subspecialty certificate; ABNM Nuclear Medicine is a separate primary physician certification. This fellowship title is not itself a board. The two boards’ eligibility pathways differ and must be confirmed individually.
medical.boardEligibilityNotice: Independent self-study does not confer ABR or ABNM eligibility, an ACGME completion certificate, medical licensure, NRC/Agreement State authorized-user status, supervised patient-care/procedure experience, or examination admission. ABR and ABNM requirements are board- and programme-specific. The Harvard Joint page describes its own eligibility pathway; Emory states successful graduates are eligible for dual boards, but individual eligibility remains subject to the certifying boards and applicable regulatory/supervision requirements.

sourceCaveats: All YouTube runtimes came from observed public catalogue metadata on 2026-10-07. They are deduplicated by video ID; publication dates were not available from the catalogue query. Future removal, region blocking or edits can change availability.

topicGaps: The observed accessible free recording ledger is 15.573611 hours, leaving 20.426389 hours below the 36-hour target; no new recording in this audit met both free public access and observed-runtime requirements.

Adult oncologic PET/CT interpretation, non-FDG tracers, appropriateness, response assessment, structured reporting and infection/inflammation remain without a complete duration-verified public teaching sequence; episode MED-002-EXPLAIN-002 teaches only an introductory reasoning framework.

The ASNC/EANM safeguards are sourceable, but there is no verified long-form public recording that covers the complete cardiac amyloidosis domain; episode MED-002-EXPLAIN-003 does not replace current protocol or expert review.

Theranostics patient selection, indications, toxicity management, longitudinal monitoring, post-therapy imaging and multidisciplinary practice lack a complete current duration-verified series; episode MED-002-EXPLAIN-004 is a limited label-reading lesson, not a clinical curriculum.

Required hands-on radiation-safety, written-directive experience, authorized-user attestation and supervised patient care cannot be supplied by self-study or online video; episode MED-002-EXPLAIN-005 explains boundaries only.

practiceQuestions.stem: Fictional case: A patient with increased ventricular wall thickness has bone-avid tracer uptake that appears grade 2 on planar imaging. Which additional evaluation is required to avoid treating this uptake as pathognomonic for ATTR cardiac amyloidosis?

options.text: Serum and urine immunofixation plus serum free light-chain testing
Only a repeat planar image at a later visit
Only a coronary calcium score
No additional evaluation because grade 2 confirms ATTR

practiceQuestions.rationale: ASNC/EANM says a monoclonal process should be excluded with serum and urine immunofixation and serum free light-chain assay irrespective of scan result; grade 2/3 uptake is not sufficient alone to erase AL amyloidosis from the differential.

practiceQuestions.stem: Fictional case: Planar bone-avid cardiac imaging appears positive, but no SPECT images were obtained. What is the most important unresolved issue?

options.text: Whether activity is blood pool or true myocardial uptake
Whether the patient has coronary calcification
Whether the image contains a liver lesion
Whether PET/MR would remove all need for laboratory testing

practiceQuestions.rationale: The ASNC/EANM practice points state that SPECT is necessary in positive planar scintigraphy to distinguish blood-pool from myocardial activity and avoid overlap.

practiceQuestions.stem: Fictional referral: An adult has PSMA-positive metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer, has received androgen-receptor pathway inhibitor therapy, and is considered appropriate to delay taxane chemotherapy. Before considering the 2025 FDA-expanded Pluvicto indication, which imaging-based selection approach is described by FDA?

options.text: Use Locametz or another approved PSMA PET product to assess tumour PSMA expression
Use a post-therapy Lu-177 distribution image as the initial selection test
Use any positive bone scan without PSMA imaging
Use serum PSA alone

practiceQuestions.rationale: FDA’s 2025 notice specifies selection using Locametz or another approved PSMA PET product based on tumour PSMA expression. This is a label-summary question, not treatment advice.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which fictional patient description matches the disease group named in the 2024 LUTATHERA label?

options.text: A patient age 12 or older with somatostatin receptor-positive gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumour
Any patient with a painful bone metastasis regardless of primary tumour
Any patient with PSMA-positive prostate cancer
Any patient with a thyroid nodule

practiceQuestions.rationale: The 2024 label names adult and paediatric patients 12 years and older with somatostatin receptor-positive GEP-NETs, including foregut, midgut and hindgut tumours. Verify the current label at point of care.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement most accurately preserves the labelled indication qualifier for radium Ra-223 dichloride in the cited FDA label?

options.text: It is indicated for castration-resistant prostate cancer with symptomatic bone metastases and no known visceral metastatic disease
It is indicated for all painful bone metastases from any cancer
It is indicated for PSMA PET-positive disease irrespective of metastatic site
It is a diagnostic tracer for initial prostate staging

practiceQuestions.rationale: The cited label limits the indication to CRPC with symptomatic bone metastases and no known visceral metastatic disease. It does not support the broader claims in the other choices; current labelling must still be checked.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which topic is explicitly included in the ABR nuclear-radiology study guide’s physics/radioisotope-safety category?

options.text: Unsealed byproduct material procedures requiring a written directive, including specified oral I-131 and parenteral radionuclide administrations
Only MRI pulse-sequence optimization
Only pathology grossing technique
Only general ultrasound physics

practiceQuestions.rationale: The ABR guide specifically lists written-directive procedures, including oral radioiodine below and above 1.22 GBq (33 mCi) and parenteral alpha/beta/photon-emitting radionuclides, within its outline.

practiceQuestions.stem: Under the standard ABR nuclear-radiology subspecialty route described on the ABR page, which combination is required before applying?

options.text: An ABR general radiology/DR/IR-DR certificate plus one year of ACGME- or RCPSC-accredited nuclear-radiology fellowship or nuclear-medicine residency training, among other requirements
Completion of this self-study course alone
A single online lecture and a state driver licence
Any research position without clinical training

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABR lists an ABR specialty certificate, one year of qualifying accredited training, a current valid medical licence and other application conditions. This independent course cannot confer eligibility.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which activity does ABNM explicitly say should not be counted toward the minimum 200 classroom/laboratory hours for radiation-safety training?

options.text: Reviewing case histories or interpreting scans
Classroom/laboratory education in radiation physics and instrumentation
Classroom/laboratory education in radiation protection
Classroom/laboratory education in mathematics for radioactivity measurement

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABNM states that reviewing case histories or interpreting scans should not count toward the 200-hour classroom/laboratory minimum, which is one component of its linked 700-hour requirements.

practiceQuestions.stem: Fictional case: A scan has grade 3 myocardial uptake and SPECT localizes uptake to myocardium. What is the most defensible educational conclusion before laboratory information is known?

options.text: Findings are strongly suggestive of ATTR, but a monoclonal process still must be excluded and results interpreted with clinical context
ATTR is proven and all laboratory tests are unnecessary
The result proves AL amyloidosis
The scan is automatically nondiagnostic because uptake is present

practiceQuestions.rationale: ASNC/EANM categorizes grade 2/3 as strongly suggestive but emphasizes that AL can show uptake and that monoclonal-protein evaluation is required.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which distinction is correct in an educational discussion of PSMA theranostics?

options.text: Diagnostic PSMA PET used for selection and post-therapy Lu-177 distribution imaging are not interchangeable modalities
A post-therapy image always replaces diagnostic PSMA PET selection
Any bone scan proves tumour PSMA expression
Theranostic eligibility can be determined from this course without clinical review

practiceQuestions.rationale: FDA’s cited Pluvicto notice directs selection with an approved PSMA PET product; a post-therapy distribution study is a different context and cannot be treated as the same selection examination.

title: Diagnostic Radiology Residency
prerequisites: Intended level: physician trainees and other advanced learners using the material only for conceptual self-study; it is not a substitute for an MD/DO curriculum or accredited residency.
Working knowledge of anatomy and basic imaging terminology is helpful.

Any clinical imaging interpretation, contrast use, procedure, urgent communication, radiation work or patient-care activity requires the applicable licence, supervision, institutional credentialing, local policy and scope of practice.
objectives: Organize diagnostic-radiology self-study by modality, anatomy, clinical question, image quality, differential and limitation.
Distinguish institutional programme pages, ACGME requirements, ABR sources, regulations, practice parameters, labels and public lectures by what each can support.
Use uncertainty-aware, differential-first fictional case reasoning without turning educational content into patient-specific advice.
Recognize image quality, radiation-protection, informatics and reporting/communication concepts at a conceptual level.
State why public video viewing cannot replace supervised clinical training, case logs, licensure, authorized-user requirements, residency completion, board eligibility or certification.
Use authentic images only through lawful, de-identified, source-linked resources with licence/provenance checked.

units.title: Imaging physics, radiation protection and informatics foundations
objectives: Connect modality physics, image quality and artifacts to cautious interpretation.
Distinguish conceptual physics study from operating equipment, performing procedures or radiation-safety authorization.
topics: x-ray interactions; CT/MR/US/nuclear physics overview; image quality; informatics; radiation biology and protection
boardDomains: ABR public Physics Study Guide: basic science; image quality/informatics; biology/protection; radiography; CT; US; MRI; nuclear medicine. The guide is not comprehensive.
units.casePractice: Use original schematic or phantom-style exercises only. Do not use patient-specific exposure, protocol or dose calculations.
units.assessment: Physics-and-artifact concept map; original questions Q02 and Q08.

units.title: Thoracic, cardiac and chest imaging reasoning
objectives: Read a chest study from technical adequacy through pattern, distribution, differential and limitation.
Recognize that emergency escalation and clinical action remain local supervised responsibilities.
topics: chest radiograph; edema/atelectasis/consolidation; ICU radiography; infection; interstitial patterns; lung nodule/mass; mediastinum; acute aorta; coronary CTA concepts
boardDomains: ABR DR public oral-transition categories include cardiothoracic imaging; this educational mapping is not an official examination blueprint.
units.casePractice: Use linked, lawfully accessible cases only; record technical limitation and differential before the impression. No image rehosting.
units.assessment: Structured fictional chest/CTA observation-to-impression exercise with a communication escalation boundary.

units.title: Emergency and trauma imaging communication
objectives: Organize a time-sensitive imaging finding into observation, limitation, communication need and documentation.
Separate image interpretation learning from trauma triage, procedures and real-time clinical decision-making.
topics: stroke-selection imaging; head/cervical/thoracolumbar trauma; blunt cerebrovascular injury; pulmonary embolism; acute aorta; blunt abdominal trauma; whole-body trauma CT
boardDomains: ABR DR Core has full-scope and noninterpretive-skills content; public post-2027 oral categories do not make this an official Core blueprint.
units.casePractice: Fictional urgent-finding communication drill only; no live on-call, patient advice, trauma protocol or treatment recommendation.
units.assessment: Original questions Q01 and Q10 plus a source-audited fictional communication note.

units.title: Neuroradiology: anatomy, pattern and differential
objectives: Use anatomy and modality limitations to produce a differential rather than overclaim a single diagnosis.
Recognize that nuclear brain findings and structural neuroimaging are complementary contexts, not interchangeable conclusions.
topics: skull base; cranial nerves; dementia and brain-neoplasm nuclear imaging; pattern/differential reasoning
boardDomains: ABR DR public oral-transition categories include neuroradiology.
units.casePractice: Use only fictional vignettes or linked authentic cases after checking source, licence and de-identification status.
units.assessment: Anatomy-to-differential table with one explicitly stated imaging limitation.

units.title: Abdominal, gastrointestinal, genitourinary and endocrine imaging
objectives: Relate modality, organ system, clinical question and limitation without presenting a protocol as patient-specific advice.
Use current source checking for contrast and appropriateness questions.
topics: esophagus; obstruction; small renal mass; prostate MRI; adrenal imaging; contrast context
boardDomains: ABR DR public oral-transition categories include abdominal imaging.
units.casePractice: For a fictional referral, name the question, possible modality limitation, and current resource to check; do not supply a patient protocol.
units.assessment: Original question Q03 and five short fictional appropriateness/source-type audits.

units.title: Hepatobiliary, pancreatic, vascular and abdominal oncology imaging
objectives: Apply structured, qualifier-aware language to liver, pancreatic, vascular and trauma imaging discussions.
Avoid conflating different organ-specific reporting systems or treating any one imaging finding as definitive outside its stated framework.
topics: chronic liver MRI; HCC/LI-RADS lecture context; cystic pancreas; cholangiocarcinoma; pancreatitis; abdominal CTA/MRA; abdominal trauma
boardDomains: ABR DR public oral-transition categories include abdominal imaging; specific reporting-system use must be verified against its current governing document.
units.casePractice: Fictional reporting exercise: document technical adequacy, observations, uncertainty and suggested correlation; no diagnostic ground-truth image is created.
units.assessment: Original question Q04 and a limitation-aware fictional liver/pancreas report.

units.title: Breast imaging and quality systems
objectives: Differentiate screening, diagnostic evaluation, ultrasound, MRI and intervention concepts at an educational level.
Explain why image interpretation or procedure competency requires supervised clinical training and applicable local requirements.
topics: mammography physics; screening controversy; interpretation; calcifications; ultrasound; MRI; intervention concepts; MQSA context
boardDomains: ABR DR public oral-transition categories include breast imaging; public programme and board sources do not make this video sequence a breast-imaging credential.
units.casePractice: Linked-only case review with case-specific rights; no procedure simulation, supervision claim or rehosted image.
units.assessment: Modality-and-limitation comparison plus original question Q09.

units.title: Pediatric imaging across systems
objectives: Frame imaging observations with age-appropriate anatomy and safety context.
Recognize why pediatric diagnostic and procedural work requires supervised specialty training.
topics: fetal/neonatal brain; airway; newborn chest; pediatric pulmonary infection; congenital heart; congenital urinary anomalies; reflux
boardDomains: ABR DR public oral-transition categories include pediatric imaging.
units.casePractice: Create a fictional age/context/differential grid; do not use it for pediatric patient selection or care.
units.assessment: Pediatric contextualization checklist and one fictional report-quality reflection.

units.title: Diagnostic nuclear medicine and hybrid imaging
objectives: Explain how functional and anatomic information may be correlated while retaining technical and biologic uncertainty.
Distinguish diagnostic education from radiopharmaceutical administration, stress testing or authorized-user activity.
topics: pulmonary nuclear medicine; perfusion SPECT; cardiac PET; PET/CT oncology; MAG3 functional assessment; infection imaging
boardDomains: ABR DR public Physics Study Guide includes nuclear medicine; the public DR sources also name nuclear imaging in the post-2027 oral category list.
units.casePractice: For fictional studies, identify functional question, anatomic correlation, artifact/limitation and non-imaging context; no tracer administration advice.
units.assessment: Original question Q05 and a hybrid-imaging limitation worksheet.

units.title: Theranostics and radionuclide-therapy evidence boundaries
objectives: Differentiate diagnostic target-expression imaging from post-therapy imaging and therapeutic administration.
State labelled indication qualifiers without turning them into individual treatment recommendations.
topics: neuroendocrine imaging; thyroid functional imaging; PSMA imaging; therapy concepts; radioiodine; Lu-177 therapies
boardDomains: ABR DR public Physics Study Guide includes nuclear medicine; public ABR DR information says Core scope includes radioisotope safety. This is not authorized-user training.
units.casePractice: Use fictional evidence-to-claim audits; current label and multidisciplinary/local review must be checked at point of care.
units.assessment: Original questions Q06 and Q07 plus a source/date audit.

units.title: Musculoskeletal imaging and technical-gap plan
objectives: Make the MSK evidence gap visible instead of assigning unmeasured viewing time.
Practice a differential-first, artifact-aware MSK reasoning framework using original conceptual materials only.
topics: MSK trauma and degenerative/inflammatory differential framework; radiograph/MR/CT modality limitations; image-quality artifacts; source and licence boundary
boardDomains: ABR DR public oral-transition categories include musculoskeletal imaging; no complete observed-duration MSK lecture ledger was retained.
units.casePractice: Use future original conceptual diagrams or link-only, lawfully accessible cases after licence review. Never create synthetic imaging as diagnostic ground truth.
units.assessment: Two planned original clips (OC01–OC02) plus a fictional modality/limitation matrix; clips count zero until rendered/probed/publicly available.

units.title: Reporting, communication, quality improvement and capstone
objectives: Write an uncertainty-aware fictional imaging impression with source type and communication boundary stated.
Distinguish a programme description, board requirement, guideline, label and learning resource before using any claim.
topics: structured reporting; preliminary/final/nonroutine communications; QI; appropriateness; contrast-source checking; image provenance; ethics and scope boundaries
boardDomains: ABR DR public information includes noninterpretive skills in Core scope; this capstone is not an official assessment or a board-readiness prediction.
units.casePractice: Capstone must use fictional vignettes or links to authentic, de-identified cases with recorded provenance and licence. No patient data, image rehosting, real-patient advice or treatment recommendation.
units.assessment: Pilot-script review, original questions Q01–Q10, and a source-audited fictional report/communication capstone.

assignment.title: Source-audited fictional multidisciplinary imaging brief
requirements: Choose two fictional vignettes from different units; do not include patient data or copied clinical images.
For each, state the clinical question, modality/technical limitation, differential, relevant source type and one boundary on the conclusion.
For one time-sensitive fictional finding, state that actual communication is governed by the responsible institution’s current policy and supervision, not this course.
For one nuclear/therapy scenario, separate diagnostic imaging, label/guideline source checking and supervised clinical responsibility.
If linking an authentic teaching case, record its source, de-identification/provenance note and licence; do not download or rehost it.
assignment.submissionBoundary: Educational work only: no real patient data, real-time triage, treatment recommendation, radiation dose/protocol calculation, procedure authorization, credentialing claim or local-policy substitute.

boardNames: American Board of Radiology (ABR) — Diagnostic Radiology certification
medical.boardStatus: ABR Diagnostic Radiology certification is distinct from residency completion. The retained ABR source describes clinical-year, accredited-training/eligible-alternate-pathway, examination, licensure and ethics conditions; public ABR sources must be checked for the applicant’s current pathway. The post-2027 oral-certifying transition is announced separately. This course is not an ABR blueprint and makes no readiness or passing claim.
medical.boardEligibilityNotice: Independent self-study does not confer ABR eligibility, ACGME residency completion, a clinical year, state medical licensure, board certification, supervised interpretation/procedure experience, case logs, institutional credentialing, authorized-user status, radiation-safety authorization, or examination admission. The cited 10 CFR pathway includes supervised work and attestation that online learning cannot provide. Confirm eligibility with ABR, the programme and applicable regulators.

originalClipPlan.title: Communicating an urgent, unexpected imaging finding — a fictional workflow pilot
objectives: Separate observation, technical limitation, uncertainty and communication boundary.
Distinguish an ACR communication framework from institution-specific operational policy.
originalClipPlan.scriptOutline:
**Title: Communicating an urgent, unexpected imaging finding — a fictional workflow pilot**

**Planned runtime:** 8 minutes. **Sources:** ACR Practice Parameter for Communication of Diagnostic Imaging Findings (revised 2025) [S14]; ABR Diagnostic Radiology certification page [S4]; ACGME DR Program Requirements [S3]. **Visuals:** original icons, a fictional report template and an abstract timing diagram only. No patient image, DICOM, dose, real patient, local escalation list, or treatment advice is used.

**00:00–00:30 — Scope.** This is independent, unaffiliated self-study. It is not on-call coverage, clinical supervision, a communication policy, accredited residency training, a credential, licence or board eligibility pathway. The visual on screen is a made-up reporting interface, not a patient record. If an actual urgent finding is encountered, follow the responsible institution’s current policy and supervised clinical chain rather than this video.

**00:30–01:15 — Why communication is part of interpretation.** A radiology report is more than a list of observations. The ACR communication practice parameter distinguishes report communication concepts including preliminary, final and nonroutine communication. The learning point is not to memorize a universal local workflow. The learning point is to pause when a finding or an uncertainty may require communication outside a routine finalized report, then use the current local policy.

**01:15–02:10 — Fictional trigger.** Consider a fictional scenario: a CT examination is being reviewed for a stated clinical question. An observation appears potentially time-sensitive, but the learner does not know the patient’s full clinical status, who is responsible, or the local escalation pathway. The correct educational first move is not to announce a definitive diagnosis. It is to separate four fields on a conceptual screen: what is observed; how technically adequate is the study; what uncertainty remains; and whether a nonroutine communication process may be needed.

**02:10–03:05 — Observation versus conclusion.** In the first field, use precise descriptive language, not a dramatic label. In the second field, make technical adequacy visible: phase, coverage, motion or other limitations can change confidence. In the third field, name the limits of inference and the relevant clinical correlation. This is a fictional reasoning exercise. It does not substitute for supervision, reviewing the source images in context, or speaking with a responsible clinician.

**03:05–04:05 — Communication is documented, not assumed.** The ACR parameter is the source for the framework, but each institution governs its own implementation. On the fictional template, the learner records that communication may be appropriate, the method contemplated, the recipient role if known, and the fact that local policy controls. The template intentionally leaves out phone numbers, time deadlines and escalation trees because inventing those details would be unsafe and institution-specific. In a real setting, the responsible radiologist and local policy determine the next step.

**04:05–05:00 — Preliminary and final reports.** A preliminary impression can support timely communication but does not eliminate the need for an accurate final report and appropriate documentation. Conversely, a signed report should not be treated as proof that every circumstance has been communicated in the way local policy requires. The educational distinction is between a report’s content, the communication process, and the clinical team’s response. This clip does not tell a learner to make a clinical call, nor does it authorize unsupervised reporting.

**05:00–05:55 — Avoid false certainty.** The hypothetical observation might have a differential. Do not invent patient facts to collapse the differential, and do not use a generated diagram as diagnostic ground truth. A safe fictional phrasing can state: “This educational scenario contains a potentially time-sensitive observation; technical and clinical correlation are required, and local communication policy should be followed.” That is deliberately less specific than a real report because this is not a real patient or a local protocol.

**05:55–06:50 — The training boundary.** The ACGME requirements describe progressive supervision and competency within an accredited training programme. The ABR certification page describes training, examination, licence and ethics conditions. Viewing a communication video—however useful—cannot provide supervised patient care, an evaluation, a case log, a licence, eligibility or certification. The same boundary applies to the original lectures in this curriculum.

**06:50–07:35 — A repeatable source check.** Before making a claim, ask: is the source a programme page, an accreditation requirement, a board rule, a practice parameter, a label, or a course lecture? Each has a different job. For a real communication decision, verify the current local policy. For a learning exercise, cite the ACR parameter, say the scenario is fictional, and leave no implication that a generic video controls local care.

**07:35–08:00 — Take-away.** Use a four-part pause: observation, technical limitation, uncertainty, and communication boundary. Then stop at the line between education and clinical responsibility. This planned clip uses only original conceptual visuals, is not yet rendered, and contributes zero verified video hours until it is rendered, duration-probed and lawfully published. Sources: ACR communication parameter, ACGME DR requirements and ABR DR certification information.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement best preserves the boundary between this course and an ABR Diagnostic Radiology eligibility pathway?

practiceQuestions.stem: Fictional course note: a learner labels every abdominal MRI reporting framework as interchangeable. Which correction is most defensible within this curriculum?

options.text: Use the HCC/LI-RADS lecture context only for its stated liver/HCC topic; do not automatically transfer an organ-specific framework to another organ without checking its current governing resource.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The retained lecture is titled “HCC Diagnosis and Application of LI-RADS.” It supports a liver/HCC context, not a blanket transfer of an organ-specific system. The course keeps qualifiers explicit rather than inventing uncited system details.

practiceQuestions.stem: Fictional case: a bone-seeking cardiac scan has uptake over the cardiac silhouette on planar imaging. What safeguard prevents treating the planar appearance alone as pathognomonic for ATTR cardiac amyloidosis?

options.text: Use SPECT to localize uptake and evaluate serum/urine immunofixation plus serum free-light chains for a monoclonal process.
Skip all correlation because any uptake proves ATTR.
Replace laboratory evaluation with a single chest radiograph.
Use a conceptual diagram as proof of diagnosis.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ASNC/EANM practice points state that SPECT is needed to distinguish blood pool from myocardial uptake in positive planar studies and call for monoclonal-protein evaluation; uptake alone is not pathognomonic for ATTR.

options.text: Diagnostic PSMA PET and post-therapy Lu-177 imaging are interchangeable.
A current label and qualified clinical team are relevant to therapeutic use; diagnostic target-expression imaging and post-therapy imaging should not be collapsed into one modality claim.
A self-study course can authorize radiopharmaceutical administration.
Any painful metastasis has the same therapeutic indication.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The retained PLUVICTO label is used for current indication/safety qualifiers. This course distinguishes diagnostic and post-therapy contexts and does not provide administration or patient-specific treatment advice.

options.text: It is a blanket indication for all painful bone metastases from any cancer.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The retained prescribing information states the CRPC, symptomatic bone-metastasis and no-known-visceral-metastasis qualifiers. This is a source-literacy question, not treatment advice; current labelling must be verified.

title: Interventional Radiology Residency
prerequisites: Medical-school-level anatomy, physiology, pathology, pharmacology, and imaging foundations.
Ability to critically read current guidelines and understand that observations in videos may be historical.
For genuine clinical work: appropriate accredited training, supervision, institutional privileges, and local policies; these are not supplied here.
objectives: Explain IR as a longitudinal clinical specialty rather than a collection of techniques.
Organize consult, imaging, safety, procedure, documentation, and aftercare questions for fictional scenarios.
Map topical study to published ABR/IR oral domains while recognizing that full diagnostic-radiology Core breadth remains outside this specialty sequence.
Audit older public lectures against current authoritative sources rather than applying them as present-day practice.
Use authentic de-identified image resources only within their stated licences and never invent patient imaging.

assignment.title: Fictional multidisciplinary IR case portfolio

unitMap.text: IR/DR as a clinical imaging specialty
Patient safety, quality, contrast and radiation protection
Image guidance, access, instruments and basic percutaneous procedures
Arterial disease, aorta, embolization and hemorrhage
Venous, thromboembolic and lymphatic care
Dialysis access and longitudinal vascular care
Interventional oncology and renal ablation
Portal, hepatobiliary and GI interfaces
Genitourinary and reproductive interventions
Pain, palliation and clinical follow-through
Pediatric IR, vascular anomalies and lymphedema
IR/DR board-aware synthesis and evidence appraisal

topicGaps: No video sequence can supply supervised procedural technique, clinical judgment, admission/consult responsibility, case logs, or credentialing.
The ABR Qualifying (Core) Exam has broad DR domains. This IR-focused course supplies selective common foundations, not a complete DR Core course.
Many selected SIR RFS webinars date from 2012–2015; they are retained for foundational/topic teaching but must be date-checked against current guidance before clinical use.
Paediatric, neurointerventional, transplant, and advanced device-specific content are introductory/selective rather than comprehensive.
No patient-specific advice, medication/dose, or therapeutic authorization is included.
remainingGaps.clinicalSkills: Supervised accredited clinical training is not supplied by these videos.

boardNames: American Board of Radiology (ABR) Interventional Radiology/Diagnostic Radiology (IR/DR) certification
ABR Diagnostic Radiology Qualifying (Core) Examination
ABR IR/DR Certifying Examination (current process through 2028; DR Oral + IR Oral announced for 2029 completers)
medical.boardStatus: IR/DR is an ABR certification pathway. It is not a separate fellowship-only board. The ABR remains authoritative; certification process and dates change.
medical.boardEligibilityNotice: This curriculum does not establish eligibility. ABR currently requires accredited clinical-year and integrated or independent IR residency pathways, passing exams, licensure, and other requirements. Starting with June 2029 IR residency completers, ABR announced DR Oral plus IR Oral; verify the live ABR page before acting.

officialProgrammes.name: Interventional Radiology (IR/DR) Residency
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: Public directory: ACGME accredited and listed as six years. The linked programme page describes integrated-IR/ESIR exposure and a clinical model. It does not publish a complete lecture set or make self-study equivalent to residency.

officialProgrammes.name: Interventional Radiology Residency
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: Public site describes broad image-guided clinical areas and locations. Its pathway page describes a five-year integrated residency following a transitional-year internship, independent IR up to two years after DR, and ESIR. It does not publish a complete didactic video curriculum.

officialProgrammes.name: Mass General Brigham Interventional Radiology-Integrated Residency
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: Official directory-listed institutional variant; a full internal rotation or lecture curriculum was not verified in the directory discovery.

medical.programmeSourceScope: Institutional pages establish publicly listed programme scope only. ACGME requirements establish accreditation standards, while ABR pages establish certification eligibility/exams. They are distinct sources and neither is replaced by this course.
sourceCaveats: Video durations were observed from public YouTube channel/search/playlist metadata. Direct automated player probing later encountered intermittent bot challenges; the ledger links canonical public URLs, but availability may change and no media is embedded or rehosted.

The IR Education channel self-identifies as a SIR RFS webinar repository. Other public channels are third-party/academic sources; inclusion is not institutional endorsement or proof that a lecture reflects current guidelines.

The Johns Hopkins directory’s six-year listing can include the clinical year, whereas ACGME describes 60 months of integrated DR/IR education after the fundamental clinical year. The course reports both without harmonizing them into a new claim.
ABR timing and certification content are evolving. The 2029 change is an announcement, so learners must recheck ABR before relying on it.
Free-to-view images are not automatically reusable. The course links resources and requires case-level licence/provenance review.

topicGaps: No video sequence can supply supervised procedural technique, clinical judgment, admission/consult responsibility, case logs, or credentialing.
The ABR Qualifying (Core) Exam has broad DR domains. This IR-focused course supplies selective common foundations, not a complete DR Core course.
Many selected SIR RFS webinars date from 2012–2015; they are retained for foundational/topic teaching but must be date-checked against current guidance before clinical use.
Paediatric, neurointerventional, transplant, and advanced device-specific content are introductory/selective rather than comprehensive.
