practiceQuestions.stem: In a fictional fluoroscopically guided intervention, which planning action most directly reduces unnecessary irradiated field size while preserving the clinical task?

options.text: Increase magnification for the entire case.
Collimate to the anatomy of interest and reassess as the task changes.
Move the detector farther from the patient to create more space.
Keep a wide field so that no anatomy is missed.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Collimation is a core dose-optimization practice. Technique must still be individualized and supervised; this question does not authorize a procedure.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional IR service is writing a safety workflow for image-guided drainage. Which sequence best reflects the clinical-practice manual’s broad process?

options.text: Procedure first; review imaging and aftercare only if a complication occurs.
Referral management, pre-procedure planning, procedure/team communication, monitoring, and written aftercare.
Imaging review only; the referring team owns all follow-up.
Schedule the procedure before confirming equipment and support.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The CIRSE manual presents a stepwise clinical pathway that includes referral, planning, performance, monitoring, and aftercare. Local policy and supervision govern practice.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which feature is specifically included in the ACR–SIR–SPR drainage/aspiration practice parameter’s published structure?

options.text: A universal medication dose table.
Specifications for monitoring/resuscitation equipment, documentation, radiation safety, and quality improvement.
A guarantee that every collection should be drained.
A replacement for local credentialing and supervision.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The parameter’s navigator includes procedure specifications, monitoring/resuscitation, documentation, radiation safety, and quality improvement. It does not make individual treatment decisions.

practiceQuestions.stem: Under the current ACGME integrated-IR requirements, which statement is accurate?

options.text: The integrated curriculum is 36 total months with no required diagnostic-radiology concentration.
The integrated curriculum consists of 60 months of DR and IR education; PGY-2–4 include 36 months concentrated in DR and the final 24 months focus primarily on IR.
No clinical-year experience is required before residency.
Residents may interpret without direct supervision from their first radiology day.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The ACGME requirement specifies 60 months, 36 DR-concentrated months in PGY-2–4, and final 24 months primarily IR. This self-study course cannot meet those requirements.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional referral for acute arterial bleeding is discussed in an IR conference. What is the most defensible next learning step before naming a procedure?

options.text: Choose an embolic agent solely from a webinar slide.
Clarify haemodynamic status, source/anatomy, imaging, contraindications, alternatives, and the multidisciplinary/supervised plan.
Assume all haemorrhage has the same arterial approach.
Skip review of prior imaging because angiography answers every question.

practiceQuestions.rationale: IR is a clinical, consultation-based specialty. The manual emphasizes review of prior investigation, patient evaluation, planning, communication, and aftercare.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement best represents responsible learning about IVC filters?

options.text: A historical lecture alone establishes the indication for any patient.
Filter decisions should be reviewed against current guideline evidence, the VTE context, anticoagulation issues, retrieval planning, and multidisciplinary care.
A filter automatically removes the need to consider anticoagulation.
Retrieval planning is irrelevant once a device is placed.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The SIR multidisciplinary clinical-practice guideline is the appropriate current evidence reference. The course does not provide patient-specific filter advice.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional dialysis-access referral has recurrent dysfunction. Which framing best fits IR’s longitudinal clinical role?

options.text: Treat it as an isolated image without history or follow-up.
Integrate symptoms, access history, imaging, multidisciplinary input, procedure planning if appropriate, and documented follow-up.
Use a publicly available webinar as a credential to perform an intervention.
Assume a single image determines all access management.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The clinical-practice manual describes IR as responsible for evaluation, planning, communication, and aftercare, not merely technical execution.

practiceQuestions.stem: For a fictional patient with HCC being considered for locoregional therapy, which dataset is most appropriate to assemble before a tumour-board discussion?

options.text: Tumour burden, liver dysfunction, performance status, staging imaging, and relevant multidisciplinary input.
Only a single unenhanced CT image.
Only the proceduralist’s preferred modality.
A promise that one locoregional technique is universally best.

practiceQuestions.rationale: AASLD emphasizes documented tumour burden, liver function, performance status, staging, and multidisciplinary management. TACE and TARE choices are not interchangeable or individually prescribed here.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement is most appropriate when a learner reviews UFE, postpartum-haemorrhage embolization, or PAE lectures?

options.text: A video establishes patient-specific candidacy.
These topics require current evidence, local expertise, patient goals, imaging, alternatives, and supervised multidisciplinary decision-making.
Reproductive considerations are outside IR consultation.
All pelvic embolization indications are identical.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The course treats these as educational, context-dependent topics. SIR’s current-guidance index should be checked alongside local policy; no case-specific recommendation follows from this question.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional patient is referred for cancer-pain intervention. Which element should be present before an IR option is discussed?

options.text: A procedure selection without knowing the patient’s goals.
A goal-of-care, symptom, imaging, safety, alternative-treatment, and follow-up discussion with the appropriate team.
An assumption that image guidance alone defines benefit.
A plan to omit aftercare communication.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The CIRSE manual frames IR as patient-focused clinical care involving evaluation, communication, monitoring, and aftercare.

practiceQuestions.stem: According to the ABR’s announced change, what applies to IR/DR residents completing training in June 2029?

options.text: Only the discontinued computer-based IR/DR Certifying component.
The DR Oral Exam and the IR Oral Exam, in addition to the unchanged Qualifying (Core) Exam process.
No assessment of diagnostic-radiology knowledge.
Automatic certification after watching a lecture course.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABR states that the 2029 process requires passing both DR Oral and IR Oral; the computer-based certifying component ends after 2028. Check ABR for updates.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which is the accurate limitation of this independent curriculum?

options.text: It completes an ACGME IR residency after 36 video hours.
It can support structured self-study but does not replace accredited training, supervised procedures, case logs, licensure, board eligibility, or certification.
It guarantees a passing ABR score.
It grants radiation-safety authorization.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ACGME requirements and ABR eligibility include formal accredited training and examinations. Videos and questions are neither clinical training nor a passing predictor.

mapping.name: Adult Critical Care Fellowship
mapping.publicCurriculumNotes: Official page: one year, ACGME accredited, seven positions. Core exposure centers on SICU 16 beds, Weinberg ICU 20 beds, and Cardiac Surgical ICU 15 beds, with more than 9000 patient-days from adult surgical services. It names daily lectures, multidisciplinary journal club, M and M, performance improvement, research forums, case conference, fellow seminar, ultrasound month, simulation workshops, and electives in neuro, cardiac, cardiac-surgical, medical/pulmonary critical care plus nephrology, ID, TEE, liver transplant and imaging. Hawaii, Bermuda, and Pakistan are opportunities, not guarantees. No complete public lecture inventory, exact didactic-hour ledger, personal procedure/case volume, or board-eligibility guarantee is published.

unitMap.text: ICU orientation, physiologic reasoning, and first hour prioritization
Shock, hemodynamics, and resuscitation
Airway, respiratory failure, ventilation, and ARDS
Renal failure, acid-base, electrolytes, and renal support
Sepsis, infection, stewardship, and source control
Cardiovascular and perioperative critical illness
Neurologic, endocrine, and metabolic emergencies
Hematology, transfusion, trauma, and surgical critical illness
GI, liver, nutrition, obstetric, and special populations
Analgesia, sedation, delirium, toxicology, and liberation
Procedures, critical-care ultrasound, and procedural safety
Ethics, communication, quality, research, and recovery

topicGaps: Hopkins has no public complete lecture inventory/exact didactic-hour ledger; rotations/conferences are not video hours.
Recordings are heterogeneous; several predate 2026 and many are third-party/international. SSC 2026, ATS 2024, SCCM 2025/2026, and AHA 2025 sources govern clinical claims.
Qualitative gaps: obstetric ICU, GI/liver/abdominal catastrophe, ethics/medico-legal/DEI, formal biostatistics/QI, and local credentialing.
Public metadata established listed free access/runtimes, but playback can change by platform/geography.
remainingGaps.clinicalSkills: Supervised accredited clinical training is not supplied by these videos.

medical.boardStatus: The assigned Johns Hopkins programme is a real separate one-year ACGME-accredited Anesthesiology Critical Care Medicine fellowship, not a directory category and not a board certificate. The ABA public CCM blueprint is used only to organize independent study. This is not an ABA, ABEM, ABS, ABIM, ACGME, or Johns Hopkins product.
medical.boardEligibilityNotice: Do not infer eligibility from the fellowship name, directory, course, or a rotation. Hopkins quick facts list anesthesiology, surgery, or emergency medicine residency, while detailed eligibility text on the same page specifies anesthesiology or surgery; seek written programme confirmation. For ABEM diplomates, ABA/ABEM state ABEM certification, four months of prior critical-care training during EM residency, an ACGME ACCM fellowship, and an additional 12 months of prospectively ABA-approved ACCM training at the same site. Hopkins lists two-year opportunities but does not establish that any design is ABA-approved. ABS SCC is separate and requires primary surgical certification before award. ABIM CCM has distinct internal-medicine and Department-of-Medicine training pathways. This course confers none of these.

officialProgrammes.institution: Johns Hopkins School of Medicine / Johns Hopkins Medicine Department of Anesthesiology and Critical Care Medicine
officialProgrammes.name: Adult Critical Care Fellowship
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: Official page: one year, ACGME accredited, seven positions. Core exposure centers on SICU 16 beds, Weinberg ICU 20 beds, and Cardiac Surgical ICU 15 beds, with more than 9000 patient-days from adult surgical services. It names daily lectures, multidisciplinary journal club, M and M, performance improvement, research forums, case conference, fellow seminar, ultrasound month, simulation workshops, and electives in neuro, cardiac, cardiac-surgical, medical/pulmonary critical care plus nephrology, ID, TEE, liver transplant and imaging. Hawaii, Bermuda, and Pakistan are opportunities, not guarantees. No complete public lecture inventory, exact didactic-hour ledger, personal procedure/case volume, or board-eligibility guarantee is published.

medical.programmeSourceScope: Actual programme, not category. Independent study scope is adult multidisciplinary ICU reasoning with anesthesia CCM public blueprint alignment, preserving surgical-ICU context. Distinct from Hopkins Pulmonary and Critical Care and Hopkins Surgical Critical Care/Acute Care Surgery. Listed combined critical-care opportunities and a non-ACGME ultrasound add-on are variants/opportunities only, not separate verified certification tracks. Pediatric critical care excluded.
sourceCaveats: No accreditation status beyond cited official pages is independently adjudicated.
No programme, board, or source endorsed this course.
No source is used to promise acceptance, certification, employment, procedural competence, or exam success.
Clinical recommendations change; date check is 2026-10-07.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional ICU patient has hypotension after surgery. Which framing best supports safe reasoning?

options.text: Assume sepsis from lactate alone.
Classify shock mechanisms, integrate serial data, and reassess.
Use one static CVP to determine volume status.
Wait for every result before escalation.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Shock is mechanistically heterogeneous. The original item tests structured synthesis, not a treatment order.

practiceQuestions.stem: For fictional moderate-to-severe ARDS, which statement reflects ATS 2024 boundaries?

options.text: Prolonged recruitment maneuvers are routinely recommended.
Higher PEEP with recruitment maneuvers is for every hypoxemic patient.
Higher PEEP without prolonged recruitment maneuvers is suggested in moderate-to-severe ARDS.
VV-ECMO is for every ARDS patient.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ATS suggests higher PEEP without prolonged LRMs in moderate-to-severe ARDS and recommends against prolonged LRMs; selection and context remain essential.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement is consistent with SSC 2026 for possible sepsis?

options.text: One biomarker rules sepsis in or out.
Collect cultures as soon as possible and ideally before antimicrobials without inappropriate delay.
qSOFA alone is the preferred hospital screen.
Wait for cultures before resuscitation.

practiceQuestions.rationale: SSC calls sepsis a clinical diagnosis and says treatment/resuscitation begins immediately.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional ventilated adult is agitated and inattentive. Which approach avoids a category error?

options.text: Equate all agitation with delirium.
Assess pain sedation delirium immobility and sleep as distinct interacting domains.
Ignore sleep and mobility until extubation.
Use one video as medication policy.

practiceQuestions.rationale: PADIS covers distinct but related domains; local policy and clinician assessment govern real care.
practiceQuestions.domain: Specialized areas: pain pharmacology ICU management

practiceQuestions.stem: Which claim matches the SCCM CCUS focused update?

options.text: CCUS replaces clinical assessment in arrest.
CCUS is suggested in septic shock acute dyspnea/respiratory failure and cardiogenic shock with stated evidence limits.
CCUS is contraindicated in volume assessment.
Image acquisition establishes competence.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The guideline makes conditional scenario-specific suggestions and notes evidence limits. It does not confer credentialing.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional ABEM diplomate asks about ACCM certification. Which is accurate?

options.text: Any one-year ICU fellowship automatically establishes eligibility.
ABEM certification and a specified approved ACCM pathway are required.
An ABIM fellowship automatically confers ABA ACCM certification.
Watching this course substitutes for fellowship verification.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The published ABA/ABEM route has credential and prospectively approved training requirements, including additional training for the specified route.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which is an appropriate first-pass approach to fictional ICU oliguria?

options.text: Assume intrinsic renal failure from one creatinine.
Integrate perfusion/volume trajectory exposures obstruction risk and serial acid-base/electrolytes.
Select dialysis from a lecture without local input.
Treat urine output as unrelated to hemodynamics.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The ABA outline includes pre-, intrinsic-, and post-renal mechanisms and acid-base/electrolyte analysis.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement about the assigned Hopkins programme is supported?

options.text: It is a generic directory category.
It is a one-year ACGME-accredited Adult Critical Care Fellowship with multidisciplinary focus.
It is identical to Hopkins pulmonary-critical-care fellowship.
Its rotations are recorded course lecture hours.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The official directory and page support a separate one-year ACCM fellowship. Rotations are not video time.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which is the published ABA CCM blueprint distribution?

options.text: All pharmacology.
25 percent basic pathophysiology, 62.5 percent diagnosis/management, 12.5 percent specialized areas.
The same secure items on every exam.
An independent course guarantee.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The weights are published by ABA; they do not predict secure content or certify anyone.

practiceQuestions.stem: In fictional persisting VF/pVT after repeated shocks, which learning stance aligns with AHA 2025?

options.text: Every post-shock VF means shock failure.
Consider recurrence versus true shock failure and follow current team algorithm/device context.
Double-sequential shocks are universally proven superior.
Pad position is irrelevant.

practiceQuestions.rationale: AHA discusses recurrence versus true shock failure and uncertainty around alternative shock strategies.

mapping.publicCurriculumNotes: This is a distinct, actual clinical physician fellowship—not a generic directory category. Johns Hopkins has a directory entry and departmental page for the same programme; they are one offering, not two variants. The directory identifies The Johns Hopkins Hospital, ACGME accreditation, and one year. The departmental page describes prehospital training, medical-direction mentorship, field experience, progressively graded medical control, journal club, milestones, and a publishable project. It lists longitudinal Howard County Fire and Rescue exposure; Johns Hopkins Lifeline ground/air critical-care transport; Maryland State Police Aviation Command scene transport; Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems exposure; and special-operations exposure with federal, state, and local agencies. These are clinical/field training descriptions, not lecture hours and not experiences supplied by this course.

medical.boardStatus: ABEM publicly describes an EMS subspecialty certification exam. The next listed exam is 2027 (odd-numbered years); ABEM says the 2026 Core Content applies beginning with 2027. The page displays 300 single-best-answer questions, an approximately eight-hour appointment with 6h20m testing time, and a legacy four-area distribution: Clinical Aspects 40%, Medical Oversight 30%, Quality Management/Research 15%, Special Operations 15%. The 2026 Core Content reorganized sections; do not infer a new 2027 weighting beyond ABEM publication.
medical.boardEligibilityNotice: Only ABEM/AOBEM decide individual eligibility. ABEM’s current page says candidates must be certified by an ABMS Member Board (with the current page stating AOBEM-certified physicians with EMS fellowship completion through July 1, 2027 are eligible), complete the specified training pathway, participate in continuing certification, meet ABEM medical-licensure policy, and comply with board-eligibility policy. The ABEM eligibility PDF describes successful completion of a minimum one-year ACGME-accredited EMS fellowship by the exam date. Johns Hopkins additionally lists ACGME-accredited Emergency Medicine residency completion as its programme prerequisite. This course, videos, another specialty certificate, or fellowship acceptance alone do not establish eligibility. Current web and February-2020 PDF AOBEM language differs; seek ABEM’s current individualized determination.

title: Emergency Medicine Fellowship
level: Clinical physician fellowship directory category (not a separate specialty programme)-aligned independent study
prerequisites: Intended level: advanced learners who can read medical literature and have foundational emergency-care vocabulary. It is most intelligible after an undergraduate medical/clinical foundation, but enrolment in an accredited programme is neither granted nor verified.

Baseline knowledge: anatomy, physiology, pharmacology concepts, ECG/radiograph/ultrasound fundamentals, probability, statistics, evidence appraisal, trauma-informed communication and local escalation practices.

For any clinical application, licensed clinicians must follow local protocols, supervision, scope of practice, credentialing and current authoritative guidance. Learners without that status must confine work to simulation and reading.
No real patient record, confidential QA file, protected download, proprietary board item, paid resource, patient scan or unsupervised procedure is required or permitted in the assignments.
objectives: Use the 2022 EM Model and the publicly posted QE distribution to organize—not predict—core emergency-medicine study.
Reason through time-sensitive presentations with an explicit differential, priority, reassessment trigger and disposition/consultation question.
Compare current primary guidance with older public lecture recordings and record version/date/scope limits.
Differentiate emergency-care knowledge from EMS medical oversight, disaster operations, POCUS quality/credentialing, operations, AI/informatics, research and education work.
Interpret authentic source-linked deidentified case material only within its license/terms; never rehost it or treat synthetic images as diagnostic evidence.
State exact certification and eligibility boundaries for generic EM, EMS, AEMUS, informatics and disaster medicine variants.
Design a fictional quality, research or education artifact with source citation, privacy, equity and safety limits.
Communicate uncertainty and the limits of independent study without claiming clinical competence or board readiness.

units.title: Emergency diagnostic reasoning, priorities and safe disposition
objectives: Use the 2022 EM Model domains, acuity and patient factors to structure a differential and time-sensitive plan.
Separate diagnostic reasoning, stabilization, reassessment, disposition and communication; identify uncertainty rather than manufacture certainty.
Apply a systems lens to risk, ethics and handoff without treating a video course as a credential.
boardDomains: 2022 EM Model: 1.0 Signs, Symptoms and Presentations
units.casePractice: Use only fictional vignettes to justify an acuity frame, differential, reassessment trigger and disposition discussion; no real chart review.
units.assessment: One-page structured reasoning note plus two original questions.

units.title: Airway, respiratory failure and ventilation
objectives: Recognize respiratory deterioration and connect examination, capnography and point-of-care findings to escalation reasoning.
Describe a team-based airway plan with backup, confirmation and post-procedure reassessment rather than attempting procedures unsupervised.
Interpret ventilator-waveform concepts at a conceptual level and identify when senior/specialty support is needed.
units.casePractice: Review public, lawfully available deidentified chest images only through their source page; document image limits and a differential, not a standalone diagnosis.
units.assessment: Airway contingency map and a waveform interpretation worksheet.

units.title: Cardiac emergencies and resuscitation
objectives: Distinguish shockable from nonshockable adult cardiac-arrest pathways using the current AHA algorithm.
Organize reversible-cause reasoning and post-ROSC priorities without substituting the course for local resuscitation policy.
Connect focused cardiac ultrasound observations to clinical context and quality assurance, not autonomous diagnosis.
units.casePractice: Run a paper-based arrest-algorithm table-top using a fictional rhythm sequence; no medication or procedure performance is assessed.
units.assessment: Ten-step adult-arrest algorithm annotation with source citation.

units.title: Shock, sepsis and critical-care transitions
objectives: Recognize sepsis/shock as time-sensitive syndromes while avoiding a single-test diagnosis.
Compare dynamic reassessment concepts with static findings and explain the guideline’s adult-hospital scope.
Plan escalation and ICU transition communication with explicit uncertainty.
units.casePractice: Fictional sepsis handoff: name suspected source, organ dysfunction evidence, response-to-treatment data and a reassessment plan; do not calculate a treatment order set.
units.assessment: Source-annotated sepsis reasoning brief.

units.title: Neurologic, behavioral and toxicologic emergencies
objectives: Prioritize stabilization and time-sensitive differential diagnoses in altered mental status, seizure, agitation and poisoning.
Recognize that behavioral emergency management requires safety, capacity, legal and team considerations.
Use toxicology pattern recognition as hypothesis generation, not a substitute for poison-center/local guidance.
units.casePractice: Use fictional vignettes; focus on immediate safety, reversible medical contributors, consultation and reassessment rather than restraint or medication instructions.
units.assessment: Differential-and-safety grid for two fictional presentations.

units.title: Trauma and environmental emergencies
objectives: Apply an ABCDE-style prioritization to trauma while making transport, imaging and consultation decisions explicit.
Identify environmental exposures as a distinct EM Model domain and avoid extrapolating old video details to current protocols.
Explain why field triage and disaster operations differ from hospital trauma lectures.
topics: Heat, cold, immersion and other environmental problems
units.casePractice: Use only a fictional mechanism/physiology worksheet; no patient images are invented or generated as diagnostic evidence.
units.assessment: Primary-survey prioritization and transfer-handover exercise.

units.title: Organ-system emergencies and cross-cutting diagnostics
objectives: Organize acute GI, renal/urogenital, endocrine, hematologic, cutaneous, HEENT and eye presentations by danger pattern and disposition risk.

Use current primary references for clinical decisions when lecture material predates them.
topics: Focused gallbladder, MSK and Doppler ultrasound concepts

2022 EM Model: 15.0 Renal and Urogenital Disorders

objectives: Apply age and pregnancy as EM Model modifying factors rather than treating adults as the default.

Recognize that the CDC outpatient opioid guideline has defined exclusions and does not dictate individual emergency care.

units.assessment: Age-modifier reflection and two original questions.

units.title: Point-of-care ultrasound and procedural quality
objectives: Describe the difference between technical acquisition, image interpretation, procedural use, QA and credentialing.
Map ultrasound study topics to the AEMUS content domains without claiming AEMUS eligibility.
Identify when image limitations, supervision and formal imaging are required.
topics: Cardiac, lung, gallbladder, MSK and Doppler concepts
QA, billing/coding, disposition and programme administration
boardDomains: AEMUS: physics/technical, anatomic/diagnostic, procedural, education/research, administration/quality
units.casePractice: Observe source-linked deidentified ultrasound resources only where lawful; do not upload, recreate or treat generated images as diagnostic ground truth.
units.assessment: Image-quality/uncertainty checklist and scope-of-practice reflection.

units.title: EMS, disaster medicine and incident systems
objectives: Differentiate bedside emergency care from EMS medical oversight, systems management and special operations.
Use the EMS Core Content’s four high-level areas to organize learning.
Explain the purpose of FEMA ICS-100/NIMS as a learning foundation without claiming operational credentialing or deployment readiness.
topics: Mass casualty, CBRNE and disaster management
boardDomains: ABEM EMS Core Content: clinical aspects
ABEM EMS Core Content: medical oversight
ABEM EMS Core Content: quality management/research
ABEM EMS Core Content: special operations
units.casePractice: Fictional multi-agency tabletop: assign an ICS interface question, communications uncertainty and a safe escalation step; never simulate deployment authorization.
units.assessment: ICS/EMS systems map and after-action reflection.

units.title: ED operations, quality, informatics and AI
objectives: Relate crowding, pathways, QA, QI, finance and change management to patient safety without reducing care to throughput metrics.
Distinguish AI implementation/evaluation from claims of autonomous clinical decision-making.
Describe why public curricula and a self-study course do not convey access to BIDMC datasets, QA records, software or mentored projects.
topics: QA/QI, peer review and implementation science
boardDomains: Practice-based learning and systems-based practice are educational mappings, not a separate ABEM fellowship blueprint.
units.casePractice: Use a fictional deidentified run chart and simulated workflow; do not access real QA or EHR records.
units.assessment: Small PDSA proposal with equity, safety and governance limits.

units.title: Education, research, climate and scholarly leadership
objectives: Compare the public aims of research, medical education, climate and resuscitation-research offerings without merging them into a clinical subspecialty.
Plan a transparent literature question, source hierarchy and learning portfolio.
State clearly what independent study cannot validate: clinical competence, procedures, scholarly authorship, faculty feedback or fellowship completion.
topics: Study design, biostatistics and responsible conduct
boardDomains: No separate generic 'Emergency Medicine Fellowship' ABEM blueprint exists.
units.casePractice: Create a fictional research-protocol critique; do not submit IRB material, use patient data or claim scholarly credit.
units.assessment: Annotated source ledger and a non-clinical capstone concept note.

assignment.title: Source-annotated emergency-care systems portfolio (independent, non-clinical)
components: A five-field reasoning note for four fictional vignettes: acuity, differential, immediate team/escalation question, reassessment and disposition uncertainty.
A source ledger comparing one public lecture claim with a current primary source; record publication/access date, scope, conflicting guidance and what cannot be concluded.

One fictional deidentified PDSA, EMS/ICS tabletop, ultrasound-QA checklist, research critique or curriculum map. No EHR, QA record, patient data, image download, IRB submission or real clinical service is used.
A 500-word boundary statement distinguishing a BIDMC directory variant from ABEM/ABMS/ACGME/EUFAC certification or accreditation claims.
assignment.submissionStandard: Cite each source URL; label all cases fictional unless using a source-linked, lawfully accessible deidentified resource; include license/terms when referring to an image. This work receives no academic credit, fellowship credit, CME, certification or clinical sign-off.

assessment.format: Formative self-assessment only: 10 original source-cited questions, four unit checklists, and portfolio rubric.
assessment.passingOrCredentialing: No passing score, proctoring, board equivalence, clinical competency sign-off, CME, affiliation or certification is awarded. Questions are original educational items, not recalled/proprietary exam material and not a validated passing predictor.

studyHours.type: transparent independent-study plan, not an equivalence claim
studyHours.note: The 36-hour video floor is met only by deduplicated public recordings with observed durations. Planned clips, clinical shifts, rotations, field exercises, reading and assignments are never converted into verified lecture hours.

mapping.name: Artificial Intelligence in Emergency Medicine
mapping.publicCurriculumNotes: 1- or 2-year option. Customized core may include AI foundations, data science/informatics, machine learning, generative AI, ED operations, decision support, governance, research, education, and leadership; includes an AI project and attending clinical work with shift reduction. Page requires completed EM residency and board certification/eligibility for applicants.

mapping.name: Climate and Human Health Fellowship
mapping.publicCurriculumNotes: Public page does not state a duration. It describes research, education, communication, policy/advocacy, optional MPH/MPP study, outside internships, and Harvard-center mentorship; it does not publish a clinical rotation schedule.

mapping.name: Fellowship in Disaster Medicine
mapping.publicCurriculumNotes: One year. Public description includes field activities, a pre-deployment course, research, hospital emergency management, CBRN, counter-terrorism medicine, EMS disaster operations, tabletop/full-scale exercises, and Boston Marathon operations. These are rotations/field experiences, not lecture hours.

mapping.name: Fellowship in Emergency Medicine Administration and Operations
mapping.publicCurriculumNotes: 1- or 2-year option with attending work at BIDMC and an HMFP affiliate with shift reduction. Weekly didactics, workshops, research time and monthly cases cover crowding, staffing, finance, pathways, QA/QI, negotiation, budgeting, change/project management, queueing, and data analysis.

mapping.name: Emergency Medical Services Fellowship
mapping.publicCurriculumNotes: One year. Includes prehospital direct care and EMT/paramedic supervision, on-scene control, optional longitudinal Boston MedFlight flying, event coverage, structured didactics/journal club, FEMA/NAEMSP coursework, and scholarship. BIDMC’s page does not itself state ACGME accreditation.

mapping.name: Emergency Medicine Research Fellowship
mapping.publicCurriculumNotes: 1- or 2-year program for board-eligible/certified emergency physicians. Describes formal epidemiology, biostatistics, trial-design, grantsmanship and writing coursework, mentored research, and clinical ED integration; it does not publish a rotation block schedule.

mapping.name: Emergency Medicine Informatics Fellowship
mapping.publicCurriculumNotes: Two years. Public page distinguishes an EM-specific track within an ACGME-accredited Multidisciplinary Clinical Informatics Fellowship from a separate non-ACGME two-year fellowship. Both combine coursework, clinical practice, lab research and mentored clinical-systems projects.

mapping.name: International Emergency Department Quality & Management Fellowship
mapping.publicCurriculumNotes: Twelve months with senior HMFP mentorship. Four public components: core curriculum, ED observation/workflow analysis, administrative and EM-training observation, and a capstone; orientation is two weeks. It is a distinct international quality/management offering.

mapping.name: Medical Education Fellowship
mapping.publicCurriculumNotes: One-year mentored fellowship; optional two-year advanced-degree route. Page describes 8–9 attending shifts/month, monthly education didactics, simulation, bedside/didactic teaching, portfolio, education research, UME/GME administration and committee work. It says SAEM-approved, not ABMS board certification.

mapping.name: Fellowship in Healthcare Quality Assurance and Quality Improvement
mapping.publicCurriculumNotes: One year. Describes QA peer review, root-cause analysis, QI/implementation science, quality metrics, decision support, weekly individualized teaching, operations meetings and research. The course does not use its confidential QA cases or patient records.

mapping.name: T32 Research Training Fellowship (Resuscitation Science, Critical Care)
mapping.publicCurriculumNotes: Two-year NIH T32 research fellowship open to eligible MDs and PhDs. It covers translational resuscitation research, clinical trials/big data/laboratory work, research boot camp, first-author project and career-development grant. It is not described as a clinical subspecialty fellowship or a clinical rotation schedule.

mapping.name: Advanced Emergency Medicine Ultrasound Fellowship
mapping.publicCurriculumNotes: One year; optional two-year advanced-degree route. Public page describes scanning, bedside teaching, image review, QA conferences, simulation, advanced echo/critical care/MSK/regional-anesthesia/procedural ultrasound, research and administration; 8–9 attending shifts/month. It states EUFAC accreditation and describes application to ABEM’s AEMUS Focused Practice Designation, subject to ABEM criteria.

topicGaps: The public lecture ledger does not replace current local procedures, supervised airway/POCUS training, patient-volume requirements or feedback.

No verified public lecture set was found that fully represents BIDMC’s individualized AI, operations, QA, research, climate or education fellowship mentoring, protected time, databases, field work or capstones. Planned clips address conceptual gaps only and count zero verified hours.

Several public lectures are commercial-channel board-review or grand-round recordings with unknown publication dates in the observed metadata. They are topic resources, not current guidelines; primary-source date/scope checking is required.
EMS/disaster study does not establish jurisdiction-specific protocols, medical-direction authority, FEMA completion, operational credentialing, security clearance or deployment readiness.

boardNames: American Board of Emergency Medicine (ABEM) — Emergency Medicine core certification
ABEM — Emergency Medical Services subspecialty certification (a separate qualifying pathway)
ABEM — Advanced Emergency Medicine Ultrasonography (AEMUS) Focused Practice Designation, not a subspecialty certificate
ABMS-approved Disaster Medicine subspecialty announced by ABEM as forthcoming; no current ABEM exam/eligibility pathway is asserted here

boardStatus.genericEntry: No ABEM, ABMS, ACGME or BIDMC source identifies a single credential or examination called ‘Emergency Medicine Fellowship.’ The supplied official BIDMC URL is a directory category linking to separate offerings.
boardStatus.coreEmergencyMedicine: ABEM says initial board eligibility follows graduation from an ACGME-, RCPSC-, or ACEM-accredited Emergency Medicine programme (or ABEM-approved combined programme) and medical-licensure compliance. Its 2022 EM Model is the basis of all ABEM exams; the public QE page provides a core EM blueprint, not a fellowship blueprint.
boardStatus.ems: EMS is a separately listed ABEM subspecialty. ABEM states candidates must meet its eligibility criteria, including ABMS certification or specified AOBEM transition provisions, a qualifying training pathway, continuing certification, licensure and other policies. BIDMC’s EMS page does not itself state ACGME accreditation, so this entry does not infer that it meets ABEM’s accredited-fellowship pathway.
boardStatus.aemus: AEMUS is an ABEM Focused Practice Designation. ABEM says programme approval is outside ACGME and EUFAC accredits training programmes. The BIDMC ultrasound page says it is EUFAC-accredited and that qualified EM graduates may apply, but ABEM independently controls eligibility and examination decisions.
boardStatus.informatics: BIDMC describes one EM-specific ACGME Multidisciplinary Clinical Informatics track and one non-ACGME route. Its page links to Clinical Informatics board content; this course does not infer individual board eligibility or equate the non-ACGME route with certification.
boardStatus.disaster: ABEM announced on 2026-03-02 that ABMS approved Disaster Medicine and said it would share updates. The current source does not publish an ABEM exam date, eligibility criteria, training pathway or a credential conferred by this study entry.
boardStatus.otherDirectoryVariants: The directory’s AI, climate, operations, research, international quality/management, medical education, QA/QI and T32 research offerings are not asserted to create an ABEM subspecialty certificate. The medical-education page says SAEM-approved; that is not represented as ABMS certification.

medical.boardEligibilityNotice: This is independent self-study only. It does not create or verify medical-school graduation, accredited residency/fellowship completion, ABEM or other board eligibility/certification, AEMUS designation, medical licensure, credentialing, supervised procedure competency, EMS medical-direction authority, clinical privileges, deployment authority, institutional affiliation or a passing result. Ask the relevant board and programme directly about current individual eligibility.

officialProgrammes.name: Artificial Intelligence in Emergency Medicine
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: 1- or 2-year option. Customized core may include AI foundations, data science/informatics, machine learning, generative AI, ED operations, decision support, governance, research, education, and leadership; includes an AI project and attending clinical work with shift reduction. Page requires completed EM residency and board certification/eligibility for applicants.

officialProgrammes.name: Climate and Human Health Fellowship
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: Public page does not state a duration. It describes research, education, communication, policy/advocacy, optional MPH/MPP study, outside internships, and Harvard-center mentorship; it does not publish a clinical rotation schedule.

officialProgrammes.name: Fellowship in Disaster Medicine
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: One year. Public description includes field activities, a pre-deployment course, research, hospital emergency management, CBRN, counter-terrorism medicine, EMS disaster operations, tabletop/full-scale exercises, and Boston Marathon operations. These are rotations/field experiences, not lecture hours.

officialProgrammes.name: Fellowship in Emergency Medicine Administration and Operations
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: 1- or 2-year option with attending work at BIDMC and an HMFP affiliate with shift reduction. Weekly didactics, workshops, research time and monthly cases cover crowding, staffing, finance, pathways, QA/QI, negotiation, budgeting, change/project management, queueing, and data analysis.

officialProgrammes.name: Emergency Medical Services Fellowship
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: One year. Includes prehospital direct care and EMT/paramedic supervision, on-scene control, optional longitudinal Boston MedFlight flying, event coverage, structured didactics/journal club, FEMA/NAEMSP coursework, and scholarship. BIDMC’s page does not itself state ACGME accreditation.

officialProgrammes.name: Emergency Medicine Research Fellowship
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: 1- or 2-year program for board-eligible/certified emergency physicians. Describes formal epidemiology, biostatistics, trial-design, grantsmanship and writing coursework, mentored research, and clinical ED integration; it does not publish a rotation block schedule.

officialProgrammes.name: Emergency Medicine Informatics Fellowship
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: Two years. Public page distinguishes an EM-specific track within an ACGME-accredited Multidisciplinary Clinical Informatics Fellowship from a separate non-ACGME two-year fellowship. Both combine coursework, clinical practice, lab research and mentored clinical-systems projects.

officialProgrammes.name: International Emergency Department Quality & Management Fellowship
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: Twelve months with senior HMFP mentorship. Four public components: core curriculum, ED observation/workflow analysis, administrative and EM-training observation, and a capstone; orientation is two weeks. It is a distinct international quality/management offering.

officialProgrammes.name: Medical Education Fellowship
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: One-year mentored fellowship; optional two-year advanced-degree route. Page describes 8–9 attending shifts/month, monthly education didactics, simulation, bedside/didactic teaching, portfolio, education research, UME/GME administration and committee work. It says SAEM-approved, not ABMS board certification.

officialProgrammes.name: Fellowship in Healthcare Quality Assurance and Quality Improvement
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: One year. Describes QA peer review, root-cause analysis, QI/implementation science, quality metrics, decision support, weekly individualized teaching, operations meetings and research. The course does not use its confidential QA cases or patient records.

officialProgrammes.name: T32 Research Training Fellowship (Resuscitation Science, Critical Care)
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: Two-year NIH T32 research fellowship open to eligible MDs and PhDs. It covers translational resuscitation research, clinical trials/big data/laboratory work, research boot camp, first-author project and career-development grant. It is not described as a clinical subspecialty fellowship or a clinical rotation schedule.

officialProgrammes.name: Advanced Emergency Medicine Ultrasound Fellowship
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: One year; optional two-year advanced-degree route. Public page describes scanning, bedside teaching, image review, QA conferences, simulation, advanced echo/critical care/MSK/regional-anesthesia/procedural ultrasound, research and administration; 8–9 attending shifts/month. It states EUFAC accreditation and describes application to ABEM’s AEMUS Focused Practice Designation, subject to ABEM criteria.

medical.programmeSourceScope: The exact BIDMC page supplied in the item packet calls itself ‘Emergency Medicine Fellowships’ and links to 12 named programmes. It is a directory CATEGORY, not an actual separate specialty programme. MED-007 transparently studies shared advanced emergency-medicine knowledge plus the public themes of those variants. It does not invent a common syllabus, accreditation, case volume, clinical rotation, certificate, or certification. Clinical rotations and field activities stated on individual pages are reported as institutional descriptions and never counted as lecture hours.
sourceCaveats: Programme pages are public descriptions, not complete syllabi, contracts, accreditation databases, lecture calendars or proof of individual eligibility.
The supplied programme page is a category directory. Names that overlap emergency medicine are retained as variants rather than falsely deduplicated into one credential.
Video duration was observed from public metadata on the stated date. Duration does not prove educational quality, currency, competence, CME or access permanence.

All clinical questions are original and all clinical cases in questions/assignments are fictional unless a source-hosted authentic deidentified resource is explicitly linked with terms. No real patient treatment advice is supplied.
Free-to-view does not imply permission to download, reproduce, modify or rehost. Read each resource’s license/terms, especially NLM/MedPix and publisher images.

originalClipPlan.title: From EM Model to a safe emergency-care reasoning note
objectives: Translate a presentation into acuity, differential, action, reassessment and disposition fields.
Show that the EM Model is a content framework, not a treatment algorithm or course credential.
originalClipPlan.scriptOutline: Original diagrams only: a five-field reasoning template, a source hierarchy and an uncertainty callout. No patient image, real chart, proprietary exam item or treatment order is used.

originalClipPlan.title: Evidence update: cardiac arrest, sepsis and the limits of protocol transfer
objectives: Contrast an AHA algorithm with the SSC adult-hospital guideline and local clinical judgment.
Teach source version/date checking and the difference between a recommendation and a legal standard.
originalClipPlan.scriptOutline: Original flow diagrams and source quotations paraphrased with citations. No dosing beyond what is publicly displayed in the cited AHA algorithm; no real patient footage.

originalClipPlan.title: POCUS quality pathway: acquisition, interpretation, QA and credentialing
objectives: Explain why learning video concepts cannot establish scanning competency or credentialing.
Map image quality, limits, documentation and QA to the public AEMUS framework.
originalClipPlan.scriptOutline: Use only original schematic probe/quality graphics and source links; never fabricate a patient scan or use an unlabeled image.

originalClipPlan.title: EMS/disaster systems: ICS interface, medical direction and after-action learning
objectives: Separate clinical care from medical oversight, systems management and special operations.
Describe ICS-100 as a foundation, not deployment or medical-direction authorization.
originalClipPlan.scriptOutline: A fictional tabletop uses fictional roles and a conceptual incident diagram; it does not enact a real emergency or provide field medical orders.

objectives: Distinguish a valid learning project from access to BIDMC systems/data or an AI clinical claim.
Use a fictional PDSA and model-evaluation checklist to frame safety, bias, privacy and escalation.
originalClipPlan.scriptOutline: Original diagrams and a fictional deidentified dashboard only. Do not use live EHR data, QA records, vendor outputs or identifiable data.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional adult patient is pulseless and the monitor shows ventricular fibrillation. Which next action best matches the 2025 AHA adult cardiac-arrest algorithm?

options.text: Deliver a shock, then resume CPR for 2 minutes.
Give epinephrine first and defer defibrillation until after two CPR cycles.
Treat as nonshockable and do not defibrillate.
Stop CPR to obtain a complete history before acting.

practiceQuestions.rationale: VF/pVT is the shockable arm of the AHA algorithm. The algorithm pairs defibrillation with high-quality CPR and rhythm reassessment; it does not support delaying the initial shock for a history. This tests an algorithmic priority, not a claim that a learner may lead resuscitation.
practiceQuestions.domain: EM Model 3.0 Cardiovascular Disorders / 19.0 Procedures & Skills

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional adult in cardiac arrest has organized electrical activity but no pulse. Which action is included in the AHA nonshockable pathway?

options.text: Epinephrine every 3–5 minutes while CPR continues and reversible causes are considered.
Immediate defibrillation as the defining first step.
Withhold oxygen until a definitive diagnosis is established.
Treat the tracing as ROSC without clinical reassessment.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The AHA algorithm directs CPR, IV/IO access, epinephrine every 3–5 minutes and consideration of advanced airway/capnography/reversible causes for asystole/PEA. Clinical teams must still use their local protocols and supervision.

practiceQuestions.stem: During a fictional PEA arrest, which option is one of the AHA algorithm’s reversible causes?

options.text: Tension pneumothorax
Uncomplicated dermatitis
Stable cataract
Chronic asymptomatic anemia alone

practiceQuestions.rationale: The algorithm’s reversible-cause list includes tension pneumothorax, along with hypovolemia, hypoxia, hydrogen ion/acidosis, hypo-/hyperkalemia, hypothermia, tamponade, toxins and pulmonary/coronary thrombosis. The question does not prescribe a procedure.
practiceQuestions.domain: EM Model 3.0 Cardiovascular Disorders / 16.0 Thoracic-Respiratory Disorders

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional adult with suspected infection has a normal initial lactate. Which interpretation is most accurate under the cited sepsis guideline?

options.text: Lactate is an adjunct; a normal value alone does not rule out sepsis.
A normal lactate definitively excludes sepsis.
Lactate should never be measured in suspected sepsis.
Only a lactate result, not clinical assessment, should determine disposition.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The guideline describes lactate as an adjunct that changes probability; it is neither sufficiently sensitive nor specific alone to rule sepsis in or out. Its recommendations address adult hospital sepsis/septic shock and cannot replace individualized clinical decision-making.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which fluid statement is most consistent with the cited Surviving Sepsis Campaign adult guideline?

options.text: Crystalloids are recommended as first-line resuscitation fluid in adults with sepsis or septic shock.
Starches are preferred as first-line fluid in all patients.
No reassessment is needed after an initial fluid decision.
The guideline creates an inflexible legal standard for every patient.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The guideline recommends crystalloids first line and recommends against starches; it also discusses dynamic measures and explicitly cannot replace clinician decision-making for individual variables. Local policy and patient context govern care.

practiceQuestions.stem: A learner says that completing this independent video sequence makes them ABEM board eligible. Which response is correct?

options.text: False; eligibility requires graduation from an ACGME-, RCPSC-, or ACEM-accredited EM program (or ABEM-approved combined program) and compliant licensure; self-study cannot meet it.
True; 36 verified video hours replace residency.
True; any BIDMC directory link automatically confers ABEM eligibility.
True; a course completion certificate replaces medical licensure.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABEM’s published criteria require qualifying residency graduation and medical-licensure compliance. This independent course neither verifies either requirement nor grants board eligibility, certification or exam access.
practiceQuestions.domain: Professional boundary / EM Model 20.0 Other Components

practiceQuestions.stem: Which high-level area is assigned the largest share of questions on ABEM’s publicly posted EMS certification examination distribution?

options.text: Clinical Aspects of EMS Medicine
Medical Oversight of EMS
Quality Management and Research
Special Operations

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABEM posts 40% for Clinical Aspects of EMS Medicine, 30% for Medical Oversight, and 15% each for Quality Management and Research and Special Operations. This is an official content distribution, not recalled exam content.

practiceQuestions.stem: In a fictional mass-casualty tabletop, what is the stated educational role of FEMA ICS-100?

options.text: It introduces ICS and provides a foundation for higher-level ICS training.
It independently authorizes field deployment as a physician.
It replaces local EMS protocols and medical direction.
It certifies a hospital’s disaster fellowship.

practiceQuestions.rationale: FEMA describes ICS-100 as an introductory independent-study course that provides the foundation for higher-level ICS training and explains the relationship between ICS and NIMS. Course study does not create deployment authority or a fellowship credential.
practiceQuestions.domain: ABEM EMS Core Content: Special Operations

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement accurately reflects BIDMC’s public Emergency Medicine Informatics Fellowship page?

options.text: It distinguishes a two-year EM-specific track within an ACGME-accredited Multidisciplinary Clinical Informatics Fellowship from a separate non-ACGME two-year fellowship.
It states that every BIDMC emergency fellowship is ACGME accredited.
It grants ABEM core certification on completion.
It describes a generic one-year Emergency Medicine Fellowship certificate.

practiceQuestions.rationale: BIDMC’s page explicitly draws this distinction. It does not turn the directory category into a single fellowship, and its statement cannot replace the certifying board’s eligibility determination.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement best distinguishes AEMUS from a generic emergency-medicine fellowship certificate?

options.text: AEMUS is an ABEM Focused Practice Designation; the ABEM page says fellowship approval is outside ACGME and identifies EUFAC as the accrediting body for training programs.
AEMUS automatically follows from watching ultrasound videos.
AEMUS is the same as ABEM core Emergency Medicine certification.
AEMUS has no eligibility or examination content requirements.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABEM labels AEMUS a Focused Practice Designation and sets separate eligibility, training-pathway and examination information. The source also lists its five content areas. It is not conferred by this curriculum.
practiceQuestions.domain: AEMUS focused practice / EM Model 19.0 Procedures & Skills

title: Emergency Medicine Residency
prerequisites: Advanced learner level: foundational anatomy, physiology, pathophysiology, pharmacology and clinical terminology (for example, senior medical student, resident, supervised clinician or equivalent).
Ability to read current English-language clinical guidance and distinguish a guideline, an institutional pathway, a board-content outline and an educational recording.
For any patient-facing activity: legal authorization, local supervision, institutional policy, required equipment/credentialing and appropriate escalation. This course supplies none of these.
No prerequisite certification is conferred or implied. Learners without a clinical background should use the course only for conceptual education and not make care decisions.
objectives: Prioritize life threats in undifferentiated presentations using a structured assessment and explicit reassessment loop.
Build a broad, acuity-aware differential and identify information that changes risk rather than anchoring on a single diagnosis.
Explain public ABEM EM Model domains, acuity frames and case-type boundaries without claiming access to protected examination content.
Use current primary guidance as the controlling source when an older educational recording conflicts or lacks date/context.
Describe emergency POCUS and procedure scope while recognizing that viewing educational material does not establish competence or permission to perform.
Communicate uncertainty, escalation needs, handoff data and patient-centered concerns in simulated cases.
State the boundaries between self-study, accredited supervised residency training, board eligibility/certification, licensure and clinical practice.

units.title: Emergency medicine frame: triage, undifferentiated presentations and safe cognitive workflow
objectives: Classify the immediate threat before pursuing a diagnostic label.
Use a structured primary assessment, focused history, reassessment and disposition loop while naming uncertainty.
topics: differential diagnosis, reassessment, handoff and documentation
boardDomains: EM Model 1.0 Signs, Symptoms and Presentations
units.casePractice: Use the ABEM simulated syncope sample as a verbal-only focused-history/differential/reassessment exercise; do not use a real patient or claim the sample is a prediction of examination performance.
units.assessment: Submit a one-page triage rationale that separates observed facts, immediate threats, differential diagnoses and safety-net disposition questions.

units.title: Resuscitation, airway and shock recognition
objectives: Recognize a deteriorating patient and prioritize team-based resuscitation actions.
Explain indications, risks, preparation and post-procedure reassessment conceptually without performing procedures unsupervised.
units.casePractice: Build a fictitious team-role checklist for a collapsing adult. State the escalation trigger, equipment check and reassessment data; no medication dose or procedural execution is assessed.
units.assessment: Timed 10-minute oral walkthrough using a non-patient mannequin/simulation prompt, graded with a checklist for prioritization, communication and reassessment.

units.title: Cardiovascular emergencies and ECG-centered reasoning
objectives: Differentiate a time-sensitive cardiovascular differential from a premature single diagnosis.
Relate ECG, symptom trajectory, perfusion and risk information to escalation and serial reassessment.
boardDomains: EM Model 1.0 Signs, Symptoms and Presentations
units.casePractice: Use a de-identified source-linked ECG or image only at its native host; write a problem representation, immediate danger list and questions for senior review.
units.assessment: Five original ECG/vignette-style multiple-choice questions plus a short rationale for why the closest alternative is unsafe or incomplete.

units.title: Respiratory and thoracic emergencies
objectives: Prioritize oxygenation, ventilation and hemodynamic assessment in acute dyspnea.
Compare obstructive, parenchymal, vascular and pleural causes using serial examination and appropriately supervised diagnostics.
topics: acute pulmonary edema and noninvasive support concepts
units.casePractice: At the host source, compare a normal and abnormal thoracic image after confirming its license and attribution. Record image limitations and a nondiagnostic alternative explanation.
units.assessment: Create a dyspnea differential map with at least one immediately life-threatening category and one reassessment measure for each branch.

units.title: Neurologic emergencies and time-critical activation
objectives: Recognize presentations that require time-sensitive stroke, seizure, infection or raised-intracranial-pressure evaluation.
Communicate last-known-well, anticoagulant/medication history, baseline function and serial neurologic change precisely.
boardDomains: EM Model 1.0 Signs, Symptoms and Presentations
units.casePractice: Use a fictional “sudden focal deficit” timeline to practice emergency activation, handoff and documentation of unknowns. Do not infer eligibility for a therapy from a course case.
units.assessment: Write a 90-second EMS-to-ED handoff with time anchors and a differential of mimics; peer-check whether any certainty was overstated.

units.title: Infection, sepsis and source-directed emergency reasoning
objectives: Identify possible infection with organ dysfunction as a high-risk trajectory requiring urgent team evaluation.
Explain how recognition, evidence-based local pathways, source evaluation, reassessment and quality measurement fit together.
boardDomains: EM Model 7.0 Head, Ear, Eye, Nose & Throat Disorders
units.casePractice: Draft a fictitious “possible sepsis” data timeline. Explicitly distinguish screening cues from diagnosis, and identify local protocol/senior-review points rather than creating a medication order.
units.assessment: Audit a fictional handoff for missing time, allergy, source, perfusion and reassessment information.

units.title: Abdominal, renal, endocrine and metabolic emergencies
objectives: Build a broad emergency differential for abdominal pain, renal/GU symptoms and metabolic derangement.
Explain why serial physiology, pregnancy status where relevant, ECG and medication context change risk assessment.
boardDomains: EM Model 5.0 Endocrine, Metabolic & Nutritional Disorders
EM Model 15.0 Renal and Urogenital Disorders
units.casePractice: Use a fictional abdominal-pain case to organize immediate threats, pregnancy-test relevance, laboratory uncertainty and a reassessment plan; no treatment calculation is required.
units.assessment: Six-item interpretation exercise that requires a differential and next information need rather than a final diagnosis alone.

units.title: Trauma, musculoskeletal injury, bleeding and burns
objectives: Apply an organized trauma primary survey and identify situations requiring immediate team escalation.
Describe immobilization, bleeding, burn and serial neurologic/perfusion assessment as supervised clinical skills.
units.casePractice: Use the WHO trauma algorithm as a reading prompt and a fictional mechanism-of-injury case. Do not use it as a substitute for ATLS, local trauma protocols or supervised care.
units.assessment: Primary-survey sequencing worksheet with a required “stop and call for help” escalation statement.

units.title: Toxicologic, environmental and exposure emergencies
objectives: Elicit exposure, formulation, route, timing, co-ingestants and toxidrome evidence without anchoring.
Identify when poison-center/toxicology and emergency services escalation are necessary.
units.casePractice: Practice an exposure history with a fictional bystander. The output is a poison-center/senior-escalation question list, not a dosing or treatment protocol.
units.assessment: Original toxicology vignette questions emphasizing time of exposure, airway/ventilation, co-ingestants and consultation.

units.title: Pediatric and obstetric emergency foundations
objectives: Adapt risk recognition, communication and equipment planning to pediatric patients and pregnancy-related presentations.
Recognize that pediatric/obstetric procedures and resuscitation require supervised competency, not video observation.
boardDomains: Pediatric age modifying factor (8% minimum in ABEM QE)
units.casePractice: Use a fictional caregiver interview to practice weight/age-aware communication, safeguarding questions and escalation. Do not calculate drug doses or perform a pediatric procedure.
units.assessment: Compare adult and pediatric triage/handoff elements in a structured table and state the supervision boundary.

units.title: Point-of-care ultrasound and procedural preparation
objectives: List the current ABEM ultrasound application categories and describe acquisition, interpretation and artifact limits.
Explain preparation, consent/risk discussion, sterile/safety checks and post-procedure reassessment at a conceptual level.
units.casePractice: At an authorized simulator or source-hosted teaching image, identify a stated view, one landmark and one limitation. No live scanning or invasive procedure is taught or authorized.
units.assessment: Annotated image-interpretation worksheet that must include a limitation and a confirmatory/escalation step.

units.title: Behavioral emergencies, communication, capacity and equity
objectives: Use de-escalating, patient-centered communication and recognize when safety, capacity or surrogate decision issues require escalation.
Explain the difference between a clinical decision and a legal determination under local law.
units.casePractice: Role-play a fictional patient-centered conversation with a peer facilitator; no real patient, recording or legal opinion is used.
units.assessment: Self-assessment using an empathy, clarification, safety and escalation checklist; instructor feedback is required for any simulated communication assessment.

units.title: EMS, disaster preparedness, quality, systems and evidence
objectives: Describe the continuum from dispatch/EMS through ED handoff, reassessment, transfer and quality review.
Interpret an emergency-care quality problem using a small, auditable measure rather than an unsupported volume benchmark.
boardDomains: ACGME systems-based practice and EMS/disaster experience
units.casePractice: Create a tabletop multi-patient prioritization exercise with fictional information. It is an educational worksheet, not a disaster command credential.
units.assessment: Submit a PDSA-style one-page proposal addressing a fictional ED handoff delay with a process measure and balancing measure.

units.title: Integrated clinical decision-making and independent-study limits
objectives: Synthesize focused history, examination, studies, prioritization, reassessment, communication and disposition in a simulated case.
State precisely which educational achievements do not establish residency completion, procedure competence, licensure or ABEM eligibility.
topics: ABEM Clinical Care and Communication/Procedure case categories
boardDomains: ABEM Certifying Exam Clinical Care Cases and Communication & Procedure Cases
units.casePractice: Complete the publicly linked ABEM Clinical Decision-Making sample only as a self-study prompt. Its named “patient” is a standardized exam scenario, not an authentic patient record or a copied test item.
units.assessment: Capstone fictional case: a written focused history/differential/study selection/reassessment/handoff plan plus a limitations statement. It is not an ABEM exam or validated predictor.

assignment.title: Source-aware emergency reasoning portfolio
deliverables: Four structured fictional case worksheets (medical resuscitation, trauma, pediatric/obstetric, toxicologic/behavioral).
One source comparison: identify the publication date and scope of an educational recording and reconcile it with a current primary guideline.

One POCUS/image worksheet using a source-hosted authentic de-identified case or licensed image; include source URL, licence/attribution check, normal/pathologic uncertainty and a statement that no scan is rehosted.
One systems/quality reflection using a fictional handoff or sepsis-recognition process measure.
assignment.safetyBoundary: No real patient data, local case logs, patient images, protected exam materials, independent procedures, prescriptions or medical orders are permitted. Fictional cases must be clearly labelled as fictional.

formative: Unit knowledge checks (the 10 original questions are examples, not a validated question bank).
Faculty/supervisor-reviewed simulated oral handoff and communication exercise where available.
Image/procedure limitation statements and source-license checks.
assessment.summativePlan: A 60-minute open-source capstone with two newly written fictional cases, a differential/prioritization/reassessment narrative, one communication task and a source/limitations declaration.
assessment.passingBoundary: There is no official pass, CME, ABEM score, residency credit, board eligibility, clinical privilege, or guarantee of examination performance. Any local instructor’s feedback is educational only.

studyHours.note: This is a transparent independent-study plan, not a clinical training-hour claim. Planned original clips count as zero ready hours until actually produced, publicly accessible and duration-probed.

mapping.institution: Johns Hopkins School of Medicine / Johns Hopkins Medicine
mapping.name: Johns Hopkins Emergency Medicine Residency
mapping.publicCurriculumNotes: Johns Hopkins describes a unique four-year residency. The public curriculum page names conferences/didactics, research, quality improvement, yearlong simulation, a longitudinal ultrasound curriculum with four weeks of dedicated ultrasound rotations, and H3EM. It labels a fourth-year Focused Advanced Specialty Training (FAST) experience. The pages retrieved do not disclose a complete rotation-by-rotation schedule or a proprietary lecture catalog, so none is invented here.

medical.boardEligibilityNotice: No course activity, video, quiz, case exercise, or pilot script confers ABEM eligibility, ABEM certification, medical licensure, hospital credentialing, residency credit, ACGME credit, procedure competence, or an affiliation.
